author: @EllisJohnson-b4h
text:
Dear Meghan,  

i have to hope you and the Netflix board  will sit together and review these comments as this would be the professional thing to do.  

The show is after all for the benefit of the paying subscribers and so these comments are crucial in understanding if you have hit the mark and given us something we want.  From the balance of the feedback on the trailer it is clear you have not. This may appear premature as it is only the trailer however it is clear it is being roundly rejected for 2 reasons.

1) Your concept
2) Your personality

1) The concept is being rejected because it is based on a phony and staged set of interactions surrounding relatively inane and generally out of touch  lifestyle advice. This is compounded by the fact the advice is being provided by someone not truly qualified to give it
.
2) the above links to your personality or at least the public perception of your "personality".  Based on the limited trailer, given the apparently banal and unoriginal nature of the "advice" people would only want to watch if they found the individual presenting it to be interesting , likeable and entertaining.  Based on all of your public interactions you appear to be none of these things.  Smiling inanely and clapping the opening of an envelope do not make you likeable as the smile has to reach the eyes for people to be convinced.

Viewers also generally reject individuals with, a lack of authenticity, a lack of self awareness, an inability to laugh at themselves and above all those who appear hypocritical.  This is clearly the perception that many have of you.

At some point you should invite yourself to truly examine why you are being rejected rather than looking for reasons why those rejecting you are either biased or simply wrong.thinking.  This level of negative feedback has to suggest you are doing something wrong  wouldn't you agree?

The areas I think you should review are as follows:

You preach to people what they should do without appearing to do it yourself 
-Charity vs personal spend

You preach to people on matters you are simply not qualified to advise on
-Cooking vs "elevating"  an at best modest acting talent

You preach women's equality rights but have appeared to desert these principals when it has suited yout agenda
- your upward marriages
- your leverage of your looks vs your talent to get ahead

You preach showing love, understanding and kindness when dealing with others but do not appear to follow these principles 
-your interactions with employees
-your interactions with your family
-your interactions with your former partners or friends 

You preach authenticity and truth but appear neither authentic or fully truthful

-you present an artifice of being the perfect person in the perfect situation which is entirely unrelatable for most people
-your show mantra does not ring true..everyone's invited....except i imagine those you've cut off
-your truth does not make it the truth, it is simply your perception or opinion which naturally comes from a biased stand point
-your single story of activism (the dish soap lecture)  appears at best embellished
-your style of interaction with others apprars to lack any truly authentic feeling

In short you preach from a lofty but very shaky lectern based on what the public perceives.  Your inability to conceive that any criticism you receive is truly valid places you in an ever shrinking echo chamber surrounded by hangers on and yes people. I would auggest this is a dangerous place to reside if you wish to be successful in the entertainment industry 

Of course it will be easier for your ego to  label this feedback as racist and misogynistic because I enjoy white male privilege.  This is of course your prerogative and so i will have to consign the writing of this to wasted time i will never get back.  Much like watching any of your endeavours to date 

Kind regards
E

text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐦 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩

Meghan Markle—the Duchess of Sussex, a title she wears like a designer handbag, all while ghosting those who dare to upset her. It’s a curious phenomenon; one moment she’s posing for heartfelt selfies with her besties, and the next, she vanishes into thin air. With a track record of treating friendships like a revolving door, she has perfected the art of disappearing when the going gets tough.

Consider the tale of her supposed close pals. There’s the loyal 𝘑𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘤𝘢 𝘔𝘶𝘭𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘺, who was once the poster child for Meghan’s inner circle. But after a minor social faux pas involving a controversial incident, Meghan decided that ghosting was in order. Just like that, Mulroney was left on read, a testament to Meghan’s precarious friendships. Who needs loyalty when you can simply cut ties with anyone who challenges your narrative?

Then there’s her frosty relationship with former castmates from 𝘚𝘶𝘪𝘵𝘴. Once a valued part of their ensemble, Meghan has exhibited all the warmth of a polar vortex since her ascent into royal life. When she didn’t receive the glowing endorsement she craved, she retreated into the shadows, leaving her former friends clutching their pearls in disbelief. They must have learned the hard way that Meghan’s concept of friendship is as fleeting as her time on the royal scene.

And while she appears to maintain a good rapport with 𝘚𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘢 𝘞𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘢𝘮𝘴 for now, one can’t help but wonder how long that will last. After all, Meghan has a knack for turning the most solid of friendships into a mere memory. Their camaraderie may be intact at the moment, but if Serena fails to meet Meghan’s expectations or offer the unwavering support she craves, will she too become a ghost in Meghan’s social portfolio?

The reality is that Meghan’s approach to friendship resembles her approach to life: superficial and self-serving. If you don’t validate her choices or fall in line with her whims, you’re out. It’s a high-stakes game of emotional roulette where the odds are stacked against anyone who dares to disagree.

The irony, of course, is that Meghan has constructed a public persona as a champion of kindness and empathy. Yet, when it comes to her friendships, that facade disintegrates faster than a knock off designer handbag. Her behaviour reveals a troubling truth: she’s less interested in fostering genuine connections and more in curating a gallery of admirers who echo her sentiments and feed her ego.

In a world that celebrates authenticity, Meghan Markle has chosen the path of the fake friend, a spectre haunting her own social landscape. It’s high time for her to face the music and realise that true friendship is built on trust and respect, not on selective appearances and strategic disappearances. If she continues down this path, she may soon find herself entirely friendless—an empty castle with no one left to turn the lights on.

Is it just me, or is there something utterly absurd about Harry and Meghan’s claim to integrity? While they love to rail against the media, they’ve turned it into their personal stage for airing grievances and sharing details best kept behind closed doors. Their high-profile chat with Oprah felt more like a prime-time soap opera than a royal disclosure, exposing family matters with all the decorum of a reality show. Trust? That’s long gone.

How can we take their complaints about media intrusion seriously when they’ve wielded the press like a weapon, crafting a narrative that’s equal parts victimhood and self-promotion? They’ve laid bare their lives in the most scandalous way imaginable, creating a spectacle out of what should have been private. It’s as if they’ve mistaken the royal family for a Netflix series, where ratings trump reality and the family business is mere entertainment.

Let’s talk about those awards, shall we? Harry’s got a Ripple of Hope Award and a shiny spot in the Living Legends of Aviation Hall of Fame. Royalty, traditionally the bestowers of honours, now seems to have entered a bizarre game of musical chairs where everyone gets a trophy for merely existing. Meanwhile, his antics and self-serving behaviour overshadow any merit these accolades might have.

The public’s reaction? Well, it’s as divided as ever. Some lap up their revelations, while others are left cringing at the sheer hypocrisy. Their willingness to exploit their royal status while claiming victimhood is a masterclass in contradiction.

And let’s not forget Harry’s military background—a legacy of service that now feels tarnished by his endless pursuit of fame. Instead of honouring that heritage, he seems hell-bent on dismantling it, trading dignity for headlines.

In the end, the combination of their media theatrics and the audacity of their royal status has cultivated a sense of betrayal that’s hard to shake off. If integrity were a currency, Harry and Meghan are already bankrupt.

So, Prince Harry has somehow found himself crowned the 25th “Hottest Man of All Time” by Harper’s Bazaar. Yes, the same Harry whose youthful charm has withered into a permanent scowl, etched deep into his face as though worn down by years of self-inflicted bitterness. He was once seen as the cheeky prince with an infectious grin, but now that grin has been replaced by a furrowed brow and a sulking demeanour. Whatever surface appeal he once had has long since been tainted by the ugliness brewing beneath.

But here’s the real stinger. Did Harry really earn this title, or was it just another strategic move in his relentless PR game? Let’s not forget that Harper’s Bazaar was the only publication granted access to his and Meghan’s recent quasi-royal tour of Colombia. You don’t need a degree in media manipulation to see what’s going on here. The Sussexes, ever the masters of controlling their narrative, didn’t let just anyone peek behind the curtain of their carefully staged escapade. And surprise, surprise—Bazaar pays back the favour by anointing Harry with this utterly preposterous accolade.

This isn’t a genuine nod to his so-called “hotness”—it’s a trade, plain and simple. A flattering headline handed out in return for exclusive access. And when you’re the only media outlet allowed to tag along for the ride, apparently you get to slap any absurd title on your subject, no matter how undeserving. Harry, “Hottest Man of All Time”? Give us a break. The man looks like he’s spent the last few years wrestling with his own demons—and losing.

In the Sussex PR universe, truth isn’t just bent—it’s strangled. The relentless need to manufacture praise, no matter how far removed from reality, has become their brand. From fawning documentaries to sycophantic interviews, every move is choreographed to feed their image. And now, with this latest stunt, they’ve stretched credibility to its breaking point. It’s not about who’s actually hot—it’s about who’s willing to sell their soul for a front-row seat to the Sussex show.

Isn’t it ironic that Prince Harry, who dove into marriage with reckless abandon, dares to critique the royal family’s choices in partners? In the first episode of the 2022 Netflix  Netflix mockumentary 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, he proclaimed that many men in the royal family are tempted to marry someone who “fits the mould” rather than someone they are truly destined to be with. Yet here he stands, the prime example of rushing into a marriage that seems more driven by lust than by genuine connection.

While his father, King Charles III, and his brother, Prince William, took the time to cultivate genuine relationships based on mutual respect, Harry raced into a union with Meghan Markle, seemingly captivated by her allure and the thrill of rebellion rather than considering the qualities that truly matter in a lifelong partner. His eagerness to act on physical attraction has resulted in a marriage riddled with drama and uncertainty, a far cry from the stability his family has achieved with their chosen partners.

Harry’s self-righteous comments drip with hypocrisy. By disparaging his relatives, he inadvertently highlights his own failure to understand the weight of his choices. In criticising others for marrying out of obligation, he has shackled himself to a partner whose ambitions and quest for notoriety overshadow the very essence of partnership.

What Harry fails to grasp is that genuine love isn’t just about physical attraction; it requires patience, understanding, and the ability to weather life’s storms together. His criticisms fall flat against the backdrop of his own tumultuous marriage, which resembles a never-ending reality show more than a committed relationship.

Perhaps it would have been better if Harry had reflected on whether his own marital experience is the shining example of love he imagines it to be before casting stones from his glass house. In his attempt to rewrite the narrative of royal romance, he has instead penned a cautionary tale about the dangers of marrying without truly knowing the person beside him. As the drama continues to unfold, it becomes increasingly clear that Harry’s critiques only serve to magnify the missteps he has made on his own rocky road of ‘love’.

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐲 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫

Once upon a time, a prince with a shiny title and a Hollywood hopeful with dollar signs in her eyes found each other and decided to live out their own ‘fairy tale’, far from the stuffy conventions of royal life. They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. Now, Harry and Meghan find themselves trapped in the palace of their nightmares, stranded in the gilded mediocrity of Montecito.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐨𝐦—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞

To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

And let’s not forget the family drama that unfolds like a soap opera on an endless loop. Harry and William, once the picture of closeness, are now estranged, a rift that seems destined to deepen. For Meghan, her fairy tale of becoming part of the Windsor family dissolved into a tabloid reality far from the idyllic promise. Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐫—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐒𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐲

So, here we are, at the “miserably ever after.” Harry and Meghan, no longer the royal rebels they once seemed but rather wannabe celebrities stuck in a loop of their own making. In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

text:
𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐲 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫

Once upon a time, a prince with a shiny title and a Hollywood hopeful with dollar signs in her eyes found each other and decided to live out their own ‘fairy tale’, far from the stuffy conventions of royal life. They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. Now, Harry and Meghan find themselves trapped in the palace of their nightmares, stranded in the gilded mediocrity of Montecito.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐨𝐦—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞

To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

And let’s not forget the family drama that unfolds like a soap opera on an endless loop. Harry and William, once the picture of closeness, are now estranged, a rift that seems destined to deepen. For Meghan, her fairy tale of becoming part of the Windsor family dissolved into a tabloid reality far from the idyllic promise. Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐫—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐒𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐲

So, here we are, at the “miserably ever after.” Harry and Meghan, no longer the royal rebels they once seemed but rather wannabe celebrities stuck in a loop of their own making. In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.

The end.    credit for this writing goes to the wanton wench.

Prince Harry, the lad who once charmed a nation, has managed quite the transformation: from beloved royal to poster boy for betrayal. In centuries past, he’d be dragged to the Tower with little ceremony, his name whispered with distaste over tankards of ale. Today, he basks in California sunshine, preaching authenticity while ghosting the very traditions that made him. Truly, a modern traitor for modern times.

For what else could we call a prince who has traded his duty for Netflix deals, swapped family loyalty for public therapy sessions, and thrown his heritage to the wind in favour of a victim narrative? Picture it: Harry, once a soldier in Afghanistan, now waging a different sort of war—a tireless battle against his own past, as he sits in his Montecito mansion. Gone are the days of duty and decorum; now it’s all about the next “revelation,” the next family gripe aired to anyone still willing to listen.

Of course, there’s Meghan, sharing in this saga as if they’re star-crossed lovers in a production of 𝘙𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘶𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘵: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. Together, they’ve built an empire on carefully curated angst, dressing up their defection as a noble quest for “freedom.” And yet, one can’t help but wonder if Harry’s “freedom” really amounts to little more than a gilded cage of their own making.

Meanwhile, back in Britain, Prince William quietly shoulders the legacy Harry discarded, preparing himself for kingship. His royal path is steady, measured—a role fulfilled with grace. Harry, on the other hand, seems more determined to stamp his name as a rogue prince, thumbing his nose at history as he clings to the fleeting rewards of his rebellion.

If Harry hoped to cement himself as some romantic figure, a maverick hero for the ages, he’s sorely mistaken. Instead, he’s  joined a long list of deserters and disgraced figures, his place in history etched not with respect but with regret. Because at the end of the day, there’s little noble in betrayal, no honour in disloyalty, and no lasting glory in the desertion of one’s own family. For a modern prince, he’s carved out a legacy steeped in treachery—one that history will neither forget nor forgive.     credit for writing goes to the wanton wench.

It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐍𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐦

In a world that seems to worship the grandiose, few individuals exemplify the essence of narcissism quite like Meghan Markle. The erstwhile actress, now the Duchess of Sussex, has turned her life into a perpetual performance, and we are all unwilling spectators in her ongoing melodrama.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐰𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝𝐲: 𝐂𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬!

From the moment she entered the royal spotlight, Meghan made it clear she intended to be the headline act. The Oprah Winfrey interview was a masterclass in self-pity, shifting the focus from the monarchy to her own perceived suffering. It’s as if she believes her struggles warrant a Netflix series—a tawdry soap opera filled with tears and accusations.

𝐂𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐂𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐬: 𝐋𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞!

Meghan has transformed the media into her personal soapbox, scripting her narrative like a desperate writer. She unleashes well-timed leaks to cast herself as the misunderstood outsider battling an archaic institution. Instead of rising to the occasion during royal turmoil, Meghan threw a tantrum on international television, crafting an image so far removed from reality it resembles fantasy.

𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐬? 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐈𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞!

In Meghan’s world, relationships are expendable. Her estrangement from her father and half-siblings reads like a bad drama. She keeps only those who serve her narrative, including her infamous rift with the royal family—an institution she clearly disdains. If she isn’t the centre of attention, she seems to lose interest, leaving a trail of broken connections.

𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠

Meghan’s relentless pursuit of fame is astounding. She traded royal duties for Hollywood deals faster than you can say “publicity stunt,” signing multi-million-pound contracts while lamenting her loss of privacy. Does she care for philanthropy, or is her true love the fleeting high of applause?

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐎𝐥𝐲𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐬: 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐏𝐢𝐭𝐲

While advocating for social issues, Meghan’s approach often feels like a marketing strategy rather than genuine concern. Each speech draws more attention to her trauma than the causes she claims to support. It’s hard to take seriously a woman who has lived in palaces while positioning herself as a martyr, using her platform for personal grievances rather than the greater good.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 — 𝐀 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐆𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐠𝐞

Meghan Markle serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of narcissism. In her quest for independence and recognition, she has alienated herself from those who might offer her support. It begs the question: in a world filled with adoration and applause, will she ever find the genuine connections she seems so desperately to seek? For all her talk of freedom and authenticity, Meghan remains trapped in a gilded cage of her own making, where the pursuit of fame ultimately leaves her more isolated than ever.

And while the world watches her every move, one thing is certain: Meghan Markle is the star of her own show, and it’s a performance that reveals far more about her character than she would like to admit.   credit for writing to the wanton wench.

author: @AliceMoon-e2f
text:
IMPROVED trailer, on Meg’s behalf: In an idyllic, overly staged home straight out of a catalog, with childlike crayon masterpieces strategically pinned to the stainless steel fridge, Meghan welcomes her dearest lifelong friends—you know, the ones who magically appeared after her wedding. Harry, dutifully playing the role of charming host, pours organic kombucha mocktails, and the group toasts to Meghan’s latest masterpiece: her very own show. Outside, in the perfectly manicured garden, Doria keeps the kids engaged in a game of hide-and-seek, their laughter conveniently muffled behind a privacy hedge.

Meghan, the epitome of warmth and authenticity, rolls up her sleeves (designer, of course) to whip up gluten-free, keto-friendly, farm-to-table pizzas alongside her besties, all while sharing inspirational anecdotes about self-discovery. “This dough,” she muses, “represents the journey of rising, just like I have.” After dinner, she leads everyone on a soul-stirring walk through her chicken coop, dispensing life lessons like, “Even chickens lay golden eggs if they believe in themselves.”

As the night winds down, Oprah beams in via Zoom, wearing her signature glasses and a mildly amused expression, to read a passage from The Bench—or as some might call it, the IKEA manual of children’s books. It’s heartfelt, it’s poetic… it’s also oddly familiar. The guests exchange polite nods, clearly grappling with the déjà vu of recycled ideas, while Meghan sits back, glowing under the soft halo of self-admiration.

It’s all so perfect, so inspiring, so utterly detached from reality. The cameras fade out, capturing one final scene of Meghan lovingly pointing at a scripted affirmation on the wall: “I am the change the world needs.” The audience? Still trying to figure out who this was actually for.

author: @PinkyPromise007
text:
Here are several actions and controversies often cited as contributing to Meghan Markle’s polarizing reputation:

1. Allegations of Bullying Staff
	•	Multiple former royal aides accused Meghan of bullying during her time at Kensington Palace, with claims of high turnover rates among her staff. Buckingham Palace even launched an investigation, though the findings were never made public.

2. Feud with the Royal Family
	•	Meghan’s tension with the royal family, especially her relationship with Kate Middleton and perceived snubs toward Queen Elizabeth II, became publicized. Reports of her making Kate cry over bridesmaid dresses contrasted with Meghan’s claims in her Oprah interview that she was the one who cried.

3. The Oprah Winfrey Interview
	•	While it gained support from some, the interview also led to significant backlash. Critics pointed out inconsistencies in her statements, including the claim that her son Archie was denied a title due to racism, despite royal protocols being the actual reason.

4. Accusations of Opportunism
	•	Meghan and Harry were accused of monetizing their royal connections through multimillion-dollar deals with Netflix, Spotify, and book deals, which some saw as exploiting the royal family while criticizing them publicly.

5. Netflix and Spotify Failures
	•	Meghan’s Spotify podcast, Archetypes, failed to deliver significant engagement, and the couple’s Netflix documentary was criticized for being overly self-indulgent. Their content was reportedly underwhelming and did not meet expectations.

6. Plagiarism Claims
	•	Meghan was accused of plagiarizing her children’s book The Bench, with critics pointing out similarities to an earlier publication.

7. Fabricated or Exaggerated Claims
	•	Critics allege Meghan has a habit of bending the truth, from questionable timelines in her Oprah interview to the claim that she had no knowledge of the royal family before meeting Harry.

8. Moonbump and Surrogacy Rumors
	•	Rumors surrounding her pregnancies, including claims of using a surrogate or wearing a prosthetic “moon bump,” have persisted and caused a storm of online speculation.

9. Public Disinterest
	•	Despite their high-profile projects, public engagement with Meghan and Harry’s content has waned. Their overexposure and perceived hypocrisy (preaching privacy while courting media deals) alienated many.

10. Perceived Exploitation of Titles
	•	Meghan and Harry’s continued use of their Duke and Duchess titles while criticizing the institution that granted them has been called hypocritical.

11. Overreliance on the Victim Narrative
	•	Many critics argue that Meghan constantly frames herself as a victim, whether of the royal family, the press, or racism, while showing little accountability for her own actions.

12. Unrelatable Lifestyle
	•	Meghan’s attempts to present herself as relatable, such as advocating for “small joys” while living in a $14 million mansion, often fall flat.

13. Inconsistent Persona
	•	Meghan has struggled to define her personal brand, shifting between being a royal, a philanthropist, a podcaster, and now a lifestyle guru, which some see as unauthentic and opportunistic.

These actions and controversies have created a divisive figure, admired by some but deeply mistrusted by others.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐀 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐭𝐨𝐫: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲

Prince Harry, the lad who once charmed a nation, has managed quite the transformation: from beloved royal to poster boy for betrayal. In centuries past, he’d be dragged to the Tower with little ceremony, his name whispered with distaste over tankards of ale. Today, he basks in California sunshine, preaching authenticity while ghosting the very traditions that made him. Truly, a modern traitor for modern times.

For what else could we call a prince who has traded his duty for Netflix deals, swapped family loyalty for public therapy sessions, and thrown his heritage to the wind in favour of a victim narrative? Picture it: Harry, once a soldier in Afghanistan, now waging a different sort of war—a tireless battle against his own past, as he sits in his Montecito mansion. Gone are the days of duty and decorum; now it’s all about the next “revelation,” the next family gripe aired to anyone still willing to listen.

Of course, there’s Meghan, sharing in this saga as if they’re star-crossed lovers in a production of 𝘙𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘶𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘵: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. Together, they’ve built an empire on carefully curated angst, dressing up their defection as a noble quest for “freedom.” And yet, one can’t help but wonder if Harry’s “freedom” really amounts to little more than a gilded cage of their own making.

Meanwhile, back in Britain, Prince William quietly shoulders the legacy Harry discarded, preparing himself for kingship. His royal path is steady, measured—a role fulfilled with grace. Harry, on the other hand, seems more determined to stamp his name as a rogue prince, thumbing his nose at history as he clings to the fleeting rewards of his rebellion.

If Harry hoped to cement himself as some romantic figure, a maverick hero for the ages, he’s sorely mistaken. Instead, he’s  joined a long list of deserters and disgraced figures, his place in history etched not with respect but with regret. Because at the end of the day, there’s little noble in betrayal, no honour in disloyalty, and no lasting glory in the desertion of one’s own family. For a modern prince, he’s carved out a legacy steeped in treachery—one that history will neither forget nor forgive.

𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝟏

Isn’t it ironic how someone so intent on preaching kindness and compassion manages to leave chaos, misery, and a trail of broken spirits in her wake? Step into the twisted fairy tale of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Deceit, where behind the thin veneer of humanitarianism and “mental health advocacy” lies a woman now branded with more monikers than she can count. Whether we call her the Dictator in Heels, Princess Pinocchio, or the Duchess Difficult, one thing is clear—her reign has been far from the fairy tale she so desperately wants us to believe.

Let’s peel back the layers, shall we?

𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬

The carefully constructed narrative that Meghan Markle wants us to buy is one of struggle, perseverance, and triumph. An actress on a cable TV show (𝘚𝘶𝘪𝘵𝘴, lest we forget, not exactly 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘺𝘸𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘢𝘭𝘵𝘺), she was once a nobody, waiting tables and fighting her way to stardom. But for those who worked with her before the royal wedding, it was less of a rise and more of a royal pain. While there were no formal complaints before she sashayed into Kensington Palace, whispers of her ‘high-maintenance’ behaviour circulated on set. A diva, some said. But hey, a few dramatic outbursts come with the territory of being a “leading lady,” right?

Then came her golden ticket: the royal family. What started as a fairy-tale romance quickly turned into a nightmare for those who had the misfortune of working for her.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

Let’s fast forward to 2018, just after the fairy-tale wedding to Prince Harry, where Meghan took up residence at Kensington Palace and reportedly made herself quite at home—at everyone else’s expense. In March 2021, 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘛𝘪𝘮𝘦𝘴 unleashed a bombshell report revealing bullying allegations against Meghan, dating back to her earliest days as the Duchess. Staff—those poor souls bound by duty and discretion—painted a chilling picture of life under her rule. She was, in their words, a nightmare who allegedly left personal assistants in tears, undermined their confidence, and drove more than a few to resign.

We don’t get the nickname Duchess Difficult for being warm and fuzzy, now do we?

In a world that seems to worship the grandiose, few individuals exemplify the essence of narcissism quite like Meghan Markle. The erstwhile actress, now the Duchess of Sussex, has turned her life into a perpetual performance, and we are all unwilling spectators in her ongoing melodrama.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐰𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝𝐲: 𝐂𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬!

From the moment she entered the royal spotlight, Meghan made it clear she intended to be the headline act. The Oprah Winfrey interview was a masterclass in self-pity, shifting the focus from the monarchy to her own perceived suffering. It’s as if she believes her struggles warrant a Netflix series—a tawdry soap opera filled with tears and accusations.

𝐂𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐂𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐬: 𝐋𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞!

Meghan has transformed the media into her personal soapbox, scripting her narrative like a desperate writer. She unleashes well-timed leaks to cast herself as the misunderstood outsider battling an archaic institution. Instead of rising to the occasion during royal turmoil, Meghan threw a tantrum on international television, crafting an image so far removed from reality it resembles fantasy.

𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐬? 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐈𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞!

She keeps only those who serve her narrative, including her infamous rift with the royal family—an institution she clearly disdains. If she isn’t the centre of attention, she seems to lose interest, leaving a trail of broken connections.

𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠

Meghan’s relentless pursuit of fame is astounding. She traded royal duties for Hollywood deals faster than you can say “publicity stunt,” signing multi-million-pound contracts while lamenting her loss of privacy. Does she care for philanthropy, or is her true love the fleeting high of applause?

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐎𝐥𝐲𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐬: 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐏𝐢𝐭𝐲

While advocating for social issues, Meghan’s approach often feels like a marketing strategy rather than genuine concern. Each speech draws more attention to her trauma than the causes she claims to support. It’s hard to take seriously a woman who has lived in palaces while positioning herself as a martyr, using her platform for personal grievances rather than the greater good.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 — 𝐀 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐆𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐠𝐞

Meghan Markle serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of narcissism. In her quest for independence and recognition, she has alienated herself from those who might offer her support. It begs the question: in a world filled with adoration and applause, will she ever find the genuine connections she seems so desperately to seek? For all her talk of freedom and authenticity, Meghan remains trapped in a gilded cage of her own making, where the pursuit of fame ultimately leaves her more isolated than ever.

And while the world watches her every move, one thing is certain: Meghan Markle is the star of her own show, and it’s a performance that reveals far more about her character than she would like to admit.   credit for writing to the wanton wench.

author: @mchelseama
text:
The Dunning-Kruger effect occurs when someone  significantly overestimates their own knowledge or ability in a particular area, often due to a lack of actual expertise in that field, leading them to be overly confident despite their incompetence and unable to recognize their own limitations; essentially, they believe they are much more skilled than they actually are and may resist feedback that contradicts their self-perception. 
Key characteristics of someone experiencing the Dunning-Kruger effect:
Overconfidence despite lack of skill:
They readily express strong opinions and confidently assert their knowledge even when lacking factual basis. 
Difficulty accepting criticism:
They may dismiss feedback or constructive criticism as being wrong or biased, even when coming from more experienced individuals. 
Inability to recognize their own limitations:
They lack self-awareness regarding their actual level of competence in a given area. 
Resistance to learning:
They may not actively seek out information or training to improve their skills because they believe they already know enough. 
Oversimplification of complex issues:
They may tend to simplify complex problems, underestimating their difficulty and overlooking nuances.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

author: @kansasrose2909
text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

text:
𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐠

Once upon a time, there was a prince. Not just any prince, mind you—this one was rebellious, charming, the life of every royal party. He’d been through it all: polo matches, helicopter rescues, the occasional scandal involving a Las Vegas hotel room. And then, along came the beautiful American actress, who swept him off his feet and promised a life of freedom, love, and media deals. It was, by all accounts, a modern fairy tale. Only this one seems to have ended with the prince being turned into a frog.

What started as a love story fit for the Instagram age has turned into the kind of cautionary tale you’d expect from a gossip magazine. Meghan, determined to rewrite royal history, thought she could take the charming prince, polish him up, and make him the face of a new brand. But in the process, she turned Harry—once everyone’s favourite, affable royal—into a man lost in a sea of podcast cancellations, slow-motion car ‘chases’, and public therapy sessions.

As for Meghan, the duchess who would modernise the monarchy, she quickly became better known for her rotating staff roster and pre-dawn emails than for any philanthropic deeds. Dubbed ‘Duchess Difficult’, she managed to clear out the palace quicker than Brexit negotiations. You have to hand it to her, though—who else could take a royal and transform him into a Hollywood house-husband doing mental health talks and fidgeting in interviews?

After all, it takes a certain kind of magic to convince a prince to turn his back on a literal kingdom in exchange for a deal with Spotify, only to have it go bust. And who could forget their $100 million Netflix ‘special’, where they spent hours recounting how tough life was inside royal palaces that most people would give their left arm to live in. Harry, once an army officer and people’s prince, now finds himself as a glorified extra in Meghan’s ongoing production of “Meghan’s World.”

The turning point must have been the New York ‘car chase’ debacle. What was sold as a high-octane thriller involving paparazzi turned out to be an awkward taxi ride that made the royals seem more out of touch than ever. At that point, it became clear that the fairy tale was wearing thin. No crowns, no tiaras—just two people bemoaning their lot in life from behind the gates of their $14 million mansion.

And now, with rumours swirling that their marriage is on the rocks, it’s hard not to wonder if Harry is finally seeing what the rest of us have known for a while. He thought he was getting his happily-ever-after. Instead, he’s found himself as the frog in a very one-sided fairy tale, waiting for a kiss that will never come.     credit for writing goes to the wanton wench.

𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐞'𝐬 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚'𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐧

Meghan Markle, self-styled "duchess of the people," seems to have quietly elevated herself to the role of America’s queen. No tiaras, no palaces (unless Montecito counts), and no coronation. Instead, she’s created her own version of royalty, blending celebrity and titles with a hefty Netflix deal. In her mind, she’s not just part of a royal family; she is *the* royal family.

This didn’t happen overnight. From the moment she walked down the aisle at St George’s Chapel, Meghan appeared more Hollywood than Windsor. That twinkle wasn’t the glow of a new duchess embracing regal duty—it was the gleam of someone who had just landed the lead role in a global drama. But a supporting role wasn’t enough. Meghan had bigger dreams.

From the outset, she crafted herself as the archetype of modern royalty—glamorous, relatable (if you like $14 million mansions), and oppressed by a world that "didn’t understand her." Meghan isn’t interested in the pomp of Old Blighty; she craves adulation, magazine covers, and the constant spotlight. Her royalty is less about duty and more about celebrity.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭 𝐄𝐬𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞

When Meghan and Harry left royal life for California, many thought they sought peace. Instead, they reinvented themselves as America’s answer to royalty. Setting up a multimillion-dollar media empire, they seemed to cast themselves as the new royal family of the West Coast. Meghan, especially, embraced her role as America’s princess—wronged by an archaic institution, now "finding her voice" in the land of the free.

But America already has its own royalty—Hollywood. It doesn’t follow Windsor rules; it’s ruthless, fickle, and loves a scandal more than a curated PR image. Meghan, like an ingénue, believes she can be both a Hollywood queen and a royal duchess. The trouble is, she’s not quite pulling it off.

Allow me a moment of reflection—a moment to thank South Park for saying, in blunt cartoon form, what we’ve all been thinking for far too long. It took a pair of animated misfits to finally unmask the Sussexes as the preening, privacy-loving paradoxes they are. And there they were: Harry, the wide-eyed prince who traded a crown for celebrity handshakes, and Meghan, the self-styled activist whose causes seem to end where the camera cuts. In one fell swoop, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 delivered what the world had been silently begging for: a full-throttle takedown of the Southparkles and their spectacular descent into self-parody.

Remember when these two high-tailed it out of Britain, bemoaning the shackles of royal life, only to shove their brand into every screen from Montecito to Manhattan? The escape to “freedom” quickly turned into a relentless self-promotional tour, complete with a glossy Netflix deal, weepy docu-series, and a Spotify podcast that droned on as vapidly as the platitudes they preach. Privacy, it turns out, is a state of mind—for the Sussexes, it’s one they scream about from every headline, podcast, and interview, their own echo chamber of self-pity.

𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 didn’t invent this farce; it merely held up a merciless mirror. They nailed Harry’s unearned martyrdom and Meghan’s shapeshifting causes, two perfectly polished caricatures of victimhood turned luxury brand. And what do the ‘Southparkles’ do in response? More finger-pointing, more grievances, another episode of “How the Palace Wronged Us,” as if the world hadn’t long ago tuned out. The Queen managed seventy years of scrutiny with grace, but two years of negative press have Harry and Meghan running to their lawyers—confirming that, yes, the only thing they’re actually good at is complaining.

In truth, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 gave them a rare gift: the one thing that’s been missing in the echo chamber of their own making—perspective. But, of course, Harry and Meghan can’t see the humour. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast: two people who desperately crave the spotlight, now reduced to cartoon characters in the cultural joke they can’t escape. Perhaps they should finally do us all a favour and give us the one thing they promised but never delivered—a quiet exit. Then again, where would the profit be in that?                   credit for this goes to the wanton wench.

Here is an article from the FEDERALIST==
Does Meghan Markle Want Us To Hate Her?
By: Madeline Osburn
January 06, 2025 
When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project?
There are plenty of reasons to hate Meghan Markle, so why did she just give us a whole Netflix season of more ammo? From stabbing the royal family in the back after having her entire life subsidized by British taxpayers to earning $25 million from Spotify for a few middling podcast episodes, Markle is a villainous figure who rakes in hate, not the praise and fandom she is clearly desperate for.

When Markle made her grand return to Instagram this New Year after dramatically quitting social media in 2021, it wasn’t for funsies. It was to announce and promote her new eight-part Netflix show, “With Love, Meghan.”
From the teaser trailer she shared, the series appears to be Markle’s best attempt at LARPing Martha Stewart with her celebrity pals on her $15 million Montecito compound. “I’m going to share some tips and tricks,” Markle says as she peruses the flower market and sprinkles dried flowers on top of glazed donuts.

“We’re not in the pursuit of perfection. We’re in the pursuit of joy!” she exclaims with an acute degree of inauthenticity. The copy is dripping with feigned platitudes and the images are suspiciously rife with royal ripoffs. This trailer is so cringe-inducing that it physically makes my eyes twitch.

What’s most surprising about this product is that there was no one close enough to her to wave their hands and gently guide her in the complete opposite direction. When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project? Did no one who loves her suggest a series with a bit more sympathetic angle? A reality show where she helps down-and-out folks find a new home? A docu-series where she visits small, but beautiful American cities, highlighting everyday heroes?

I’m just shooting from the hip, and these may not be streaming hits, but the fact that no one close to her advised her against her casual yet glamourous homemaker shtick (or they did and she didn’t listen) says a lot about the type of person she surrounds herself with. Ironically, that’s also what we mainly learn from the teaser trailer guest list — that Markle spends her time arranging flowers and beekeeping with some of the most affluent and out-of-touch celebrities in her Hollywood bubble. “This is probably one of the most glamourous moments of my life,” gushes Mindy Kaling.
And it’s important to clarify here that the snobbery does not come from the idea of picture-perfect homemaking. This type of nearly unattainable farm-to-table perfection is what skyrocketed and sustained Martha Stewart, Ina Garten, Ballerina Farm, and waves of Instagram influencers following in their footsteps. Women do not loathe these women for their ideas or talents. We gobble them up and strive to emulate their recipes and cabinet paint colors in our own kitchens. No, it’s the laughable idea that the privileged princess, the Hollywood actress-turned-diva-sister-in-law, and royal golddigger who excommunicated her husband from his family, is someone we trust as a source for bringing joy and life into our own homes.

The only plausible explanation for Markle’s vanity project is that she relishes victimhood so much that she doesn’t care what the haters say because their critiques and comments sustain her signature victim mentality. Knowing she will never be the beloved people’s princess like her late mother-in-law, she’s stopped trying and settled for the loathed queen of Montecito.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.   credit for this writing goes to the wanton wench.

author: @ocdman202
text:
Meghan and Harry    just  WANNABE AMERICAN ROYALTY 💥💥
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.                           credit for this writing goes to the wanton wench.

Does Meghan Markle Want Us To Hate Her?
By: Madeline Osburn
January 06, 2025 
When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project?
There are plenty of reasons to hate Meghan Markle, so why did she just give us a whole Netflix season of more ammo? From stabbing the royal family in the back after having her entire life subsidized by British taxpayers to earning $25 million from Spotify for a few middling podcast episodes, Markle is a villainous figure who rakes in hate, not the praise and fandom she is clearly desperate for.

When Markle made her grand return to Instagram this New Year after dramatically quitting social media in 2021, it wasn’t for funsies. It was to announce and promote her new eight-part Netflix show, “With Love, Meghan.”
From the teaser trailer she shared, the series appears to be Markle’s best attempt at LARPing Martha Stewart with her celebrity pals on her $15 million Montecito compound. “I’m going to share some tips and tricks,” Markle says as she peruses the flower market and sprinkles dried flowers on top of glazed donuts.

“We’re not in the pursuit of perfection. We’re in the pursuit of joy!” she exclaims with an acute degree of inauthenticity. The copy is dripping with feigned platitudes and the images are suspiciously rife with royal ripoffs. This trailer is so cringe-inducing that it physically makes my eyes twitch.

What’s most surprising about this product is that there was no one close enough to her to wave their hands and gently guide her in the complete opposite direction. When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project? Did no one who loves her suggest a series with a bit more sympathetic angle? A reality show where she helps down-and-out folks find a new home? A docu-series where she visits small, but beautiful American cities, highlighting everyday heroes?

I’m just shooting from the hip, and these may not be streaming hits, but the fact that no one close to her advised her against her casual yet glamourous homemaker shtick (or they did and she didn’t listen) says a lot about the type of person she surrounds herself with. Ironically, that’s also what we mainly learn from the teaser trailer guest list — that Markle spends her time arranging flowers and beekeeping with some of the most affluent and out-of-touch celebrities in her Hollywood bubble. “This is probably one of the most glamourous moments of my life,” gushes Mindy Kaling.
And it’s important to clarify here that the snobbery does not come from the idea of picture-perfect homemaking. This type of nearly unattainable farm-to-table perfection is what skyrocketed and sustained Martha Stewart, Ina Garten, Ballerina Farm, and waves of Instagram influencers following in their footsteps. Women do not loathe these women for their ideas or talents. We gobble them up and strive to emulate their recipes and cabinet paint colors in our own kitchens. No, it’s the laughable idea that the privileged princess, the Hollywood actress-turned-diva-sister-in-law, and royal golddigger who excommunicated her husband from his family, is someone we trust as a source for bringing joy and life into our own homes.

The only plausible explanation for Markle’s vanity project is that she relishes victimhood so much that she doesn’t care what the haters say because their critiques and comments sustain her signature victim mentality. Knowing she will never be the beloved people’s princess like her late mother-in-law, she’s stopped trying and settled for the loathed queen of Montecito.

author: @Xeg-ValkyrieDigital
text:
So, the trailer drops, and the internet immediately calls out how tone-deaf, staged, and all-around ridiculous it is. And what does she do? Flips out, claiming the marketing team put out “trash” on purpose, using bad clips to twist the narrative—and that they deserved to be fired. But if it was THAT terrible, Meghan, why did you share the exact same trailer on your shiny new Instagram?🧐🤔 

Let’s be real—she’s just upset that the global public isn’t falling for it and has no problem calling out the contradictions. Privacy? Sure… while putting herself in a clearly staged house on display, only to get mad when people notice and criticize it.

Had to circle back on this because, honestly, the whole thing is just wild. Netflix shouldn’t cave to the drama. Leave the comments on—they prove exactly why people aren’t buying into this anymore and really hit home how disliked she is. No matter the trailer, no matter how amazing it is, the principal character in the trailer is and always will be the same, which is the only problem here. 

Over a million views, and as of this post, 89% dislikes. Yeah… that feels like a pretty accurate reflection of the general disdain for her as a person overall.

Once upon a time, a prince with a shiny title and a Hollywood hopeful with dollar signs in her eyes found each other and decided to live out their own ‘fairy tale’, far from the stuffy conventions of royal life. They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. Now, Harry and Meghan find themselves trapped in the palace of their nightmares, stranded in the gilded mediocrity of Montecito.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐨𝐦—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞

To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

And let’s not forget the family drama that unfolds like a soap opera on an endless loop. Harry and William, once the picture of closeness, are now estranged, a rift that seems destined to deepen. For Meghan, her fairy tale of becoming part of the Windsor family dissolved into a tabloid reality far from the idyllic promise. Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐫—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐒𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐲

So, here we are, at the “miserably ever after.” Harry and Meghan, no longer the royal rebels they once seemed but rather wannabe celebrities stuck in a loop of their own making. In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.
