author: @kansasrose2909
text:
𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐲 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫

Once upon a time, a prince with a shiny title and a Hollywood hopeful with dollar signs in her eyes found each other and decided to live out their own ‘fairy tale’, far from the stuffy conventions of royal life. They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. Now, Harry and Meghan find themselves trapped in the palace of their nightmares, stranded in the gilded mediocrity of Montecito.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐨𝐦—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞

To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

And let’s not forget the family drama that unfolds like a soap opera on an endless loop. Harry and William, once the picture of closeness, are now estranged, a rift that seems destined to deepen. For Meghan, her fairy tale of becoming part of the Windsor family dissolved into a tabloid reality far from the idyllic promise. Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐫—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐒𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐲

So, here we are, at the “miserably ever after.” Harry and Meghan, no longer the royal rebels they once seemed but rather wannabe celebrities stuck in a loop of their own making. In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞𝐬 

Allow me a moment of reflection—a moment to thank South Park for saying, in blunt cartoon form, what we’ve all been thinking for far too long. It took a pair of animated misfits to finally unmask the Sussexes as the preening, privacy-loving paradoxes they are. And there they were: Harry, the wide-eyed prince who traded a crown for celebrity handshakes, and Meghan, the self-styled activist whose causes seem to end where the camera cuts. In one fell swoop, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 delivered what the world had been silently begging for: a full-throttle takedown of the Southparkles and their spectacular descent into self-parody.

Remember when these two high-tailed it out of Britain, bemoaning the shackles of royal life, only to shove their brand into every screen from Montecito to Manhattan? The escape to “freedom” quickly turned into a relentless self-promotional tour, complete with a glossy Netflix deal, weepy docu-series, and a Spotify podcast that droned on as vapidly as the platitudes they preach. Privacy, it turns out, is a state of mind—for the Sussexes, it’s one they scream about from every headline, podcast, and interview, their own echo chamber of self-pity.

𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 didn’t invent this farce; it merely held up a merciless mirror. They nailed Harry’s unearned martyrdom and Meghan’s shapeshifting causes, two perfectly polished caricatures of victimhood turned luxury brand. And what do the ‘Southparkles’ do in response? More finger-pointing, more grievances, another episode of “How the Palace Wronged Us,” as if the world hadn’t long ago tuned out. The Queen managed seventy years of scrutiny with grace, but two years of negative press have Harry and Meghan running to their lawyers—confirming that, yes, the only thing they’re actually good at is complaining.

In truth, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 gave them a rare gift: the one thing that’s been missing in the echo chamber of their own making—perspective. But, of course, Harry and Meghan can’t see the humour. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast: two people who desperately crave the spotlight, now reduced to cartoon characters in the cultural joke they can’t escape. Perhaps they should finally do us all a favour and give us the one thing they promised but never delivered—a quiet exit. Then again, where would the profit be in that?

Oh, the irony. Here we have the Duke and Duchess of Sussex—those self-styled champions of “privacy” who fled the royal fold to pursue their “authentic” lives—caught in the act of their true pursuit: piles upon piles of cash. Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? They only wanted privacy from the obligations, it seems—not from the cash and cameras that come with the royal titles they claim to despise.

If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

text:
𝐀 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐭𝐨𝐫: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲

Prince Harry, the lad who once charmed a nation, has managed quite the transformation: from beloved royal to poster boy for betrayal. In centuries past, he’d be dragged to the Tower with little ceremony, his name whispered with distaste over tankards of ale. Today, he basks in California sunshine, preaching authenticity while ghosting the very traditions that made him. Truly, a modern traitor for modern times.

For what else could we call a prince who has traded his duty for Netflix deals, swapped family loyalty for public therapy sessions, and thrown his heritage to the wind in favour of a victim narrative? Picture it: Harry, once a soldier in Afghanistan, now waging a different sort of war—a tireless battle against his own past, as he sits in his Montecito mansion. Gone are the days of duty and decorum; now it’s all about the next “revelation,” the next family gripe aired to anyone still willing to listen.

Of course, there’s Meghan, sharing in this saga as if they’re star-crossed lovers in a production of 𝘙𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘶𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘵: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. Together, they’ve built an empire on carefully curated angst, dressing up their defection as a noble quest for “freedom.” And yet, one can’t help but wonder if Harry’s “freedom” really amounts to little more than a gilded cage of their own making.

Meanwhile, back in Britain, Prince William quietly shoulders the legacy Harry discarded, preparing himself for kingship. His royal path is steady, measured—a role fulfilled with grace. Harry, on the other hand, seems more determined to stamp his name as a rogue prince, thumbing his nose at history as he clings to the fleeting rewards of his rebellion.

If Harry hoped to cement himself as some romantic figure, a maverick hero for the ages, he’s sorely mistaken. Instead, he’s  joined a long list of deserters and disgraced figures, his place in history etched not with respect but with regret. Because at the end of the day, there’s little noble in betrayal, no honour in disloyalty, and no lasting glory in the desertion of one’s own family. For a modern prince, he’s carved out a legacy steeped in treachery—one that history will neither forget nor forgive.

text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

text:
𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐨 𝐭𝐨 𝐙𝐞𝐫𝐨 

Prince Harry’s downfall is a masterclass in how to squander a royal legacy, trading duty for self-pity and fame for victimhood. Once a beloved prince, now he’s more like a tabloid caricature—a man perpetually aggrieved, endlessly fixated on a narrative of blame. The tragic irony? He’s the architect of his own demise.

After the spectacular mess that was 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘹𝘪𝘵, Harry and Meghan promised they were stepping back for a quiet life away from the suffocating grip of royal duties. But what followed wasn’t a retreat to the countryside—it was a relentless assault on the monarchy. In his memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦, Harry exposed the royal family’s private affairs in a way that felt less like a heartfelt confession and more like a glorified tantrum. From physical altercations with William to tales of being denied “extra sausages” at breakfast and the horror of a smaller bedroom, Harry’s grievances came off as the petulant cries of a man unable to cope with the reality of his privileged existence. His anecdotes about being deprived of a lavish lifestyle, including the shocking detail that King Charles had cut off his pocket money, painted a picture of someone intent on airing family laundry while completely missing the mark on what it means to struggle.

Not only has the British public had enough, but more people globally are seeing him in his true colours. What was once endearing—the cheeky lad in the military, the prince who walked behind his mother’s coffin with quiet dignity—has now morphed into a man perpetually at war with his own privilege. His complaints, whether about family squabbles or being told Meghan had to earn her keep, are so far removed from reality that they seem almost satirical. The grand irony, of course, is that for someone so intent on escaping the royal spotlight, Harry seems desperate to cling onto any fragment of it that remains.

The cracks in the Sussex facade are now painfully obvious. Once a united front, Harry is now appearing alone more frequently, sparking speculation that even his marriage isn’t immune to the fallout of their disastrous PR. Meghan, once touted as the modern, progressive breath of fresh air, is increasingly seen as a catalyst in Harry’s undoing—a figure whose Hollywood aspirations and woke crusades have done little but alienate her from the public she so desperately sought approval from.

Harry’s story isn’t one of triumph over adversity; it’s a cautionary tale of self-sabotage. In his quest to escape the clutches of the monarchy, he’s become more of a prisoner than ever—trapped by his own choices, his once-promising legacy reduced to little more than a footnote in royal history. And the sad truth is, the more he whinges and wallows, the less anyone seems to care.

𝐁𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐄𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐱 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲

Rumours are rife that Prince Harry has taken a decisive step: filing for divorce from Meghan. The question on everyone’s lips, though, is where he’s done it. If he’s filed in the UK, it could potentially set a legal precedent around the custody of the couple’s two children. Given British jurisdiction’s potential role, the path to securing their future may not align with Meghan’s plans, and instead, could place them squarely within the traditions of the Royal Family.

The custody implications could be profound. Should the British courts have a say, it would open up avenues for the monarchy to reassert its influence over Harry’s children — a consideration given the historic British law on the guardianship of royal heirs. This law could prove advantageous for Harry if he wants to ensure the children maintain strong ties to the UK and the royal legacy they’ve been born into.

Beyond legalities, however, the rift between Harry and Meghan might expose Meghan’s public image to scrutiny from an angle she may not have anticipated. Harry is armed with knowledge that could counter any narrative Meghan spins in the memoir, she allegedly penning. He knows, as the British say, “where the bodies are buried.” If he were to publicly challenge the version of events she has cultivated, it could complicate her carefully managed image — and potentially cast doubt on her credibility.

If Harry were to return to the royal fold, it’s likely his role would echo that of another wayward royal, Prince Andrew. Seen, but not heard. Present but sidelined. The Royal Family, ever strategic, might just see value in such an arrangement — a quiet reclamation of one of their own that simultaneously disrupts Meghan’s media campaign. The subtle reabsorption of Harry would be a shrewd way to keep family matters from further public spectacle, shielding the monarchy’s image without fanfare.

Titles, of course, are more than mere formalities. Harry could voluntarily place his dukedom into abeyance, effectively removing Meghan’s right to use the Duchess of Sussex moniker, one she has wielded with financial acumen. Should their divorce be formalised, Meghan’s “Princess Henry of Wales” style — technically derived through marriage — could be withdrawn as well. Although it’s unlikely the King would ever grant Harry another dukedom, the division would mean that Meghan’s association with royalty would no longer hold the weight it once did, relegating her permanently outside the sphere of Windsor.

While much of this remains speculative, the legal and royal mechanisms are all in place. If Harry pursues this course, he could see his children’s ties to the UK strengthened, his titles strategically managed, and his own position within the royal fold restored, albeit quietly. This would mark the end of the Sussex chapter and the beginning of a new, redefined role for Harry — one that, even if understated, reinforces his place in the monarchy and keeps Meghan on the outside.

In the latest chapter of the Sussexes’ post-palace saga, the power couple known for “escaping” the royal family’s golden cage seems to have run into a bit of a gilded problem of their own. Enter 𝘐𝘯𝘛𝘰𝘶𝘤𝘩’s newest headline: “𝘋𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘎𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘥!”—not exactly the fairy-tale ending they had in mind when they departed Britain’s shores, proclamations of independence trailing behind them.

Let’s dissect this “$100 million empire collapse,” shall we? For two people who once bemoaned the scrutiny and pressures of being in the royal fishbowl, Harry and Meghan sure seemed to make a swift U-turn back into the spotlight, albeit a more lucrative one. Who knew privacy could be so profitable? Between lucrative Netflix deals, star-studded Spotify podcasts, and tell-all book advances, they proved that fame can indeed be sold by the pound—until, it appears, the empire built on grievances and carefully crafted victimhood narratives began showing some cracks.

“𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘉𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴! screams the subhead, as if the world needed reminding of their extravagances. For Harry, the young prince who once dared to tell the world his father had financially abandoned him (while living in a multimillion-dollar Montecito mansion), financial reality may now be arriving with the grace of a stagecoach collision. As for Meghan, the transformation from a self-styled humanitarian to the Duchess of Dollar Signs has not exactly gone unnoticed.

And now, it seems, the “reckless royals” have reached the inevitable end of their fairy tale: not with the pomp and pageantry they once denounced, but with headlines about their “𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴!” Yes, the allure of billionaire ambitions was just too tantalising to resist, even for those who claimed to be fleeing the trappings of aristocratic privilege. One might say their undoing wasn’t so much greed as a relentless pursuit of relevance—wrapped in the velvet of luxury and sprinkled with a hint of delusion.

So, as the Sussex empire teeters, perhaps this isn’t the fairy tale they envisioned when they traded Buckingham Palace for a Californian castle. Instead of newfound freedom, it seems they’ve simply exchanged one gilded cage for another—only this time, the bars are forged by ambition, avarice, and a ravenous pursuit of fame.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

text:
𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐨 𝐭𝐨 𝐙𝐞𝐫𝐨    AND NOW THIS FROM MEGHAN?

Prince Harry’s downfall is a masterclass in how to squander a royal legacy, trading duty for self-pity and fame for victimhood. Once a beloved prince, now he’s more like a tabloid caricature—a man perpetually aggrieved, endlessly fixated on a narrative of blame. The tragic irony? He’s the architect of his own demise.

After the spectacular mess that was 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘹𝘪𝘵, Harry and Meghan promised they were stepping back for a quiet life away from the suffocating grip of royal duties. But what followed wasn’t a retreat to the countryside—it was a relentless assault on the monarchy. In his memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦, Harry exposed the royal family’s private affairs in a way that felt less like a heartfelt confession and more like a glorified tantrum. From physical altercations with William to tales of being denied “extra sausages” at breakfast and the horror of a smaller bedroom, Harry’s grievances came off as the petulant cries of a man unable to cope with the reality of his privileged existence. His anecdotes about being deprived of a lavish lifestyle, including the shocking detail that King Charles had cut off his pocket money, painted a picture of someone intent on airing family laundry while completely missing the mark on what it means to struggle.

Not only has the British public had enough, but more people globally are seeing him in his true colours. What was once endearing—the cheeky lad in the military, the prince who walked behind his mother’s coffin with quiet dignity—has now morphed into a man perpetually at war with his own privilege. His complaints, whether about family squabbles or being told Meghan had to earn her keep, are so far removed from reality that they seem almost satirical. The grand irony, of course, is that for someone so intent on escaping the royal spotlight, Harry seems desperate to cling onto any fragment of it that remains.

The cracks in the Sussex facade are now painfully obvious. Once a united front, Harry is now appearing alone more frequently, sparking speculation that even his marriage isn’t immune to the fallout of their disastrous PR. Meghan, once touted as the modern, progressive breath of fresh air, is increasingly seen as a catalyst in Harry’s undoing—a figure whose Hollywood aspirations and woke crusades have done little but alienate her from the public she so desperately sought approval from.

Harry’s story isn’t one of triumph over adversity; it’s a cautionary tale of self-sabotage. In his quest to escape the clutches of the monarchy, he’s become more of a prisoner than ever—trapped by his own choices, his once-promising legacy reduced to little more than a footnote in royal history. And the sad truth is, the more he whinges and wallows, the less anyone seems to care.

text:
Apparently Markle is absolutely hopping mad that Netflix haven't blocked the comments as she did in her usual cowardly manner for her rejuvenated Instagram account. I rather suspect that Netflix actually wants the cooking show to be a catastrophe so they are much better placed to end their doomed association with the Montecito moaners. By continuing to allow comments, the overwhelming majority are negative or even openly hostile, Netflix is softening up the Parkles for the inevitable termination notice and makes their decision even easier to make.
The message is clear to both Netflix and to the Parkles - Friar Tuck and his current wife's TV and film production days are over. Such is the antipathy that these two have generated by their entitled ways and the trashing of both of their families that people will take any opportunity they can to land a blow where it hurts i.e. in their wallets or take them down. text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤… 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐨𝐭𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle once declared their intention to step back from royal life, seeking a quieter existence away from the relentless media scrutiny, the invasive headlines, and the unending circus of royal duty. We all remember that moment in January 2020 when the world collectively gasped at their decision to break free from the gilded cage of monarchy. They wanted, they said, to live in peace. They craved privacy.

But fast forward to today, and one has to wonder—if privacy was truly the goal, why do Harry and Meghan constantly seek out the spotlight like moths to a flame? After all, we’ve hardly been short of the couple these past few years, have we? And every time we think they’re retreating into the shadows, back they come, brighter than ever, ready to tell us more, reveal more, and sell more.

𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐃𝐮𝐭𝐲 𝐭𝐨 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐟𝐥𝐢𝐱 𝐃𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬

When Harry and Meghan announced their “progressive new role” in early 2020, they claimed they would split their time between the UK and North America, free from the relentless scrutiny of the British press. They wanted to raise their children away from prying eyes, to live like regular people.

Well, if this is what regular people do—signing £100 million deals with Netflix—then sign me up! Because just months after their grand exit from royal life, the couple inked a lucrative contract with the streaming giant to produce documentaries, films, and television shows. Their docuseries, 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 & 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧, provided intimate glimpses of their lives—precisely the kind of exposure they once claimed to flee from.

One can only marvel at the paradox: “Please leave us alone,” they plead, while flinging open the doors to their California mansion, cameras rolling, lights flashing.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐡 𝐁𝐨𝐦𝐛𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐥

Ah, but we’re not done. Who can forget 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 interview with Oprah Winfrey in March 2021? Broadcast to millions across the globe, Harry and Meghan laid bare their grievances with the royal family in what was undoubtedly the most talked-about television moment of the year. Harry lamented the toxic tabloid culture that hounded them, but in the next breath, the couple dropped bombshell after bombshell that sent those very tabloids into a feeding frenzy.

Was this stepping away from the limelight? Hardly. This was stepping right into the fire—voluntarily.

COULD ANYTHING HAVE BEEN MORE CRUEL TO THE DYING QUEEN??
EVEN OPRAH HAS ERASED THIS INTERVIEW FROM THE INTERNET BECAUSE IT WAS SO HEARTLESS AND CRUEL. 


 ‘𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞’ 𝐔𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐚

As if the Oprah interview wasn’t enough, along came *Spare*, Harry’s tell-all memoir published in early 2023. Within its pages, Harry spilled secrets from the very heart of royal life—recollections of private conversations, moments of familial tension, and, oh yes, that infamous fight with his brother William. The book broke sales records but also shattered any remaining illusion that Harry and Meghan desired a quiet life. They weren’t running from the spotlight; they were standing squarely in its centre, microphone in hand, demanding more.

To promote ‘𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞’ Harry and Meghan embarked on a media blitz, appearing on television interviews, podcasts, and talk shows—each one more revealing than the last. Privacy? This isn’t privacy. This is public relations, plain and simple.

All the wanted was  𝐀 𝐃𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐊𝐢𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞.

Ah, Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex—what 𝐢𝐬 the truth beneath that glossy exterior? Is she the warm, genuine philanthropist championing change, or are we all witnessing a carefully constructed façade, where even the smiles appear as tightly rehearsed as a royal wave?

Take, for instance, the multitude of "fake smiles" reportedly flashed at every corner. Body language experts, with their magnifying glasses practically glued to her lips, have suggested these expressions seem less like joy and more like a polite veneer slapped on to mask her inner turmoil. You know the kind—the smile you give when your shoes pinch or, worse, when your multimillion-dollar Spotify deal is unceremoniously yanked from under you. 

One can’t help but wonder: Is this all part of the performance? Are we seeing the real Meghan, or is she merely playing a part? The cool, poised ex-royal who can handle the cruel blows of the public arena—or the fiery and determined woman, as some astrologers have hinted, forever grappling with balancing her public and private self?

Then there’s the curious dichotomy between her self-professed vulnerability and her undeniable confidence. She wants to be seen as relatable, yet she's working on projects bigger than Harry’s ginger beard—because make no mistake, darling, she 𝐢𝐬 the one wearing the trousers. Confidence, sure, but is it authentic? Or merely a Hollywood-esque masking of whatever emotional storms may be brewing underneath?

Whatever the case, Markle’s perpetual attempts to curate her image are unmistakable, making one wonder: Is she as real as a royal reality show, or are we merely buying tickets to a performance? 

But perhaps, like many in the public eye, the Duchess knows that keeping up appearances is part of the gig. After all, in a world where one’s entire brand can be undone with the flick of a tweet or, worse, a Netflix snub, who can blame her for wanting to manage the narrative? Still, one has to ask: at what point does the performance stop, and the real Meghan Markle begin?

text:
𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐨 𝐭𝐨 𝐙𝐞𝐫𝐨 

Prince Harry’s downfall is a masterclass in how to squander a royal legacy, trading duty for self-pity and fame for victimhood. Once a beloved prince, now he’s more like a tabloid caricature—a man perpetually aggrieved, endlessly fixated on a narrative of blame. The tragic irony? He’s the architect of his own demise.

After the spectacular mess that was 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘹𝘪𝘵, Harry and Meghan promised they were stepping back for a quiet life away from the suffocating grip of royal duties. But what followed wasn’t a retreat to the countryside—it was a relentless assault on the monarchy. In his memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦, Harry exposed the royal family’s private affairs in a way that felt less like a heartfelt confession and more like a glorified tantrum. From physical altercations with William to tales of being denied “extra sausages” at breakfast and the horror of a smaller bedroom, Harry’s grievances came off as the petulant cries of a man unable to cope with the reality of his privileged existence. His anecdotes about being deprived of a lavish lifestyle, including the shocking detail that King Charles had cut off his pocket money, painted a picture of someone intent on airing family laundry while completely missing the mark on what it means to struggle.

Not only has the British public had enough, but more people globally are seeing him in his true colours. What was once endearing—the cheeky lad in the military, the prince who walked behind his mother’s coffin with quiet dignity—has now morphed into a man perpetually at war with his own privilege. His complaints, whether about family squabbles or being told Meghan had to earn her keep, are so far removed from reality that they seem almost satirical. The grand irony, of course, is that for someone so intent on escaping the royal spotlight, Harry seems desperate to cling onto any fragment of it that remains.

The cracks in the Sussex facade are now painfully obvious. Once a united front, Harry is now appearing alone more frequently, sparking speculation that even his marriage isn’t immune to the fallout of their disastrous PR. Meghan, once touted as the modern, progressive breath of fresh air, is increasingly seen as a catalyst in Harry’s undoing—a figure whose Hollywood aspirations and woke crusades have done little but alienate her from the public she so desperately sought approval from.

Harry’s story isn’t one of triumph over adversity; it’s a cautionary tale of self-sabotage. In his quest to escape the clutches of the monarchy, he’s become more of a prisoner than ever—trapped by his own choices, his once-promising legacy reduced to little more than a footnote in royal history. And the sad truth is, the more he whinges and wallows, the less anyone seems to care.

𝐈𝐬 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐨𝐱𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞? 

That’s the question on everyone’s lips as the Duke of Sussex slowly, and somewhat tragically, comes to grips with the storm he’s waded into. For years, the world watched with morbid curiosity as Prince Harry fell under the spell of the cable actress who seemed to promise him the kind of liberation he thought he craved. But now, it appears the fog might be lifting.

Ever since he and Meghan Markle packed up their royal obligations and moved stateside, Harry has been like a lost puppy. Yes, he’s had the bright lights of Montecito and the comforting hum of Netflix millions to keep him warm, but let’s not pretend that anything about their lives has been a fairy tale. He’s gone from being one of the most loved members of the royal family to a footnote on the latest podcast ranking. Once a cheeky, beloved prince, he now seems diminished, frequently wielding accusations against his own flesh and blood, all in the name of “truth-telling” while sporting a perpetual look of someone who's swallowed a bee.

Of course, Meghan clings to the spotlight with the fervour of someone whose star is slowly dimming. The glossy sheen she’s worked so hard to maintain is starting to crack. But as the carefully curated image begins to crumble, people are starting to ask: Has Harry been played? The relentless pursuit of victimhood, the never-ending stream of grievances, the lawsuits, the interviews where they professed they just wanted privacy while eagerly airing their private lives—it’s all starting to look a bit tiresome, isn’t it? It’s as if Meghan brings chaos and strife wherever she goes, leaving a trail of scorched earth behind her. And now, Harry, standing alone in the ashes, might be waking up to the realisation that he’s not a leading man in a romcom. He’s the fall guy in a badly scripted melodrama.

The cracks in their fortress of solidarity are hard to ignore. From awkward public appearances where Harry looks increasingly weary, to reports of them living “separate lives,” it’s clear that the Duke of Sussex’s fairytale with the duchess might not have the happy ending he envisioned. Could it be that Harry is slowly but surely realising the poison in the air? That aligning himself so completely with Meghan’s seemingly endless vendettas has isolated him from everyone who once cared for him? The court of public opinion has shifted, and not in their favour.

Perhaps Harry is beginning to understand that the woman he thought was his greatest ally may, in fact, be his Achilles heel. Meghan’s love for the spotlight is insatiable, and Harry’s been dragged along for the ride, his own identity slowly eroded. Meanwhile, she flourishes as the victim-turned-heroine in her own fantasy, playing to the gallery of sycophants while carefully casting Harry in the role of the sacrificial lamb.

As he surveys the debris of the bridges burned and relationships fractured, one can only wonder—how much longer before Harry tires of this reality show existence? The toxicity surrounding Meghan Markle has become undeniable, but the question now is: does Harry finally see it?

author: @ocdman202
text:
“𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐲 𝐭𝐨 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲: 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐱𝐞𝐬 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐨𝐬”

It’s hard to imagine a more spectacular fall from grace. Meghan Markle, a former cable TV actress, married into the British Royal Family and found herself with a title, a global platform, and all the trappings of royalty. But this wasn’t Tinseltown—there were protocols, centuries of tradition, and an expectation to serve the British people. And here’s where the Sussexes’ story shifts from fairy tale to farce.

Let's be clear: when they first announced they were stepping back, many Brits wished them luck on their new life. Their decision to seek more privacy and independence didn’t raise many eyebrows initially. But it was their behaviour afterwards that truly soured public opinion.

What they did next is the stuff of modern hubris. First came the 𝘖𝘱𝘳𝘢𝘩 𝘪𝘯𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘷𝘪𝘦𝘸, a two-hour primetime spectacular where grievances were aired in the most public way possible. Meghan, who played the “𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘴𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘳” card at every turn, presented herself as a victim of a royal machine that allegedly ignored her mental health struggles. For Harry, it was a platform to lay bare years of family resentment, tarnishing the reputations of the very people who once adored him. Royalty, by its nature, thrives on discretion, loyalty, and service, but the Sussexes were out for blood—𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘪𝘳 narrative was all that mattered.

The whining didn’t stop there. Harry’s memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 only deepened the chasm, dragging up petty sibling squabbles with Prince William, tantrums over tiaras, and accusations that reeked of entitlement and narcissism. Once the couple cried racism and abandonment, any residual goodwill began evaporating at lightning speed.

Their behaviour screamed hypocrisy. How could they demand privacy while signing a multimillion-dollar Netflix deal to expose the very family they abandoned? Their repeated claims of victimhood wore thin—when you trade castles for Montecito mansions, it’s hard to sell yourself as oppressed. No one cared about them leaving the royal family, but they certainly cared about the Sussexes playing both sides: royal victims and Tinseltown celebrities, crying injustice while cashing in.

What’s even more damning is their irrelevance. The world has moved on. Meghan’s Spotify podcast flopped, their Netflix ventures struggled, and their post-royal projects seem like nothing more than vanity projects. Meanwhile, King Charles, William, and Catherine continue to quietly go about the business of serving the public—a stark contrast to Harry and Meghan’s continuous soap opera.

The Sussexes were handed it all, only to throw it away in a grand gesture of self-sabotage. From royal glitz to grasping at fame, their story has shifted from one of potential to one of pathos. No one forced them out, but their behaviour post-exit ensured they are never welcomed back.

author: @NewsCynic
text:
Megan Markle’s public image is a masterclass in ambition—she took the “fairy tale princess” narrative and flipped it into “reality TV meets royal drama.” If Netflix had existed in the 1500s, Anne Boleyn might have taken notes. The Duchess of Sussex has turned what could have been a quiet life of charity and tea parties into a global campaign of interviews, documentaries, and thinly veiled autobiographies. She didn’t just marry a prince; she married a platform. And let’s be honest, she’s worked harder on her brand than most royals have on their royal duties.

Her knack for self-promotion is unparalleled. From casual, Oprah couch confessions to a Spotify deal so short-lived it could be the subject of its own podcast, she’s proven that you can, in fact, complain about your privilege as long as you do it in designer clothes. She might have stepped back from royal duties, but she’s leaning all the way into Hollywood melodrama. It’s a career pivot so bold it deserves its own crown—preferably one from the prop department.

And let’s not forget the relentless quest for privacy. It’s a noble cause, but one that oddly seems to involve cameras, microphones, and a book deal. Who knew “leaving the royal spotlight” came with a lighting crew? Meghan Markle isn’t just breaking the royal mold—she’s turned it into a content factory, complete with press releases and perfectly curated Instagram moments. But hey, at least the royal family is finally getting a break... from Meghan’s version of The Crown.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

And now this cooking show fiasco,  what next?

Meghan Markle, self-styled "duchess of the people," seems to have quietly elevated herself to the role of America’s queen. No tiaras, no palaces (unless Montecito counts), and no coronation. Instead, she’s created her own version of royalty, blending celebrity and titles with a hefty Netflix deal. In her mind, she’s not just part of a royal family; she is *the* royal family.

This didn’t happen overnight. From the moment she walked down the aisle at St George’s Chapel, Meghan appeared more Hollywood than Windsor. That twinkle wasn’t the glow of a new duchess embracing regal duty—it was the gleam of someone who had just landed the lead role in a global drama. But a supporting role wasn’t enough. Meghan had bigger dreams.

From the outset, she crafted herself as the archetype of modern royalty—glamorous, relatable (if you like $14 million mansions), and oppressed by a world that "didn’t understand her." Meghan isn’t interested in the pomp of Old Blighty; she craves adulation, magazine covers, and the constant spotlight. Her royalty is less about duty and more about celebrity.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭 𝐄𝐬𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞

When Meghan and Harry left royal life for California, many thought they sought peace. Instead, they reinvented themselves as America’s answer to royalty. Setting up a multimillion-dollar media empire, they seemed to cast themselves as the new royal family of the West Coast. Meghan, especially, embraced her role as America’s princess—wronged by an archaic institution, now "finding her voice" in the land of the free.

But America already has its own royalty—Hollywood. It doesn’t follow Windsor rules; it’s ruthless, fickle, and loves a scandal more than a curated PR image. Meghan, like an ingénue, believes she can be both a Hollywood queen and a royal duchess. The trouble is, she’s not quite pulling it off.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧

Despite claiming to seek a "normal" life, Meghan clings to her royal title like a last Louis Vuitton bag on Rodeo Drive. In every appearance, she’s “the Duchess of Sussex.” Her role in American life is drenched in royal overtones—co-founding Archewell, lecturing from her Montecito mansion, and wielding her title like a sceptre.

Meghan forgets that in America, titles don’t make you royal. What works in the UK, where centuries of tradition cushion you, doesn’t fly across the Atlantic. Here, you’re only as royal as your last deal. Americans love their celebrities messy and flawed, not preachy.

AND NOW THIS LATEST FIASCO WITH THE COOKING SERIES!!


𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐖𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐬

Meghan is obsessed with her own fairytale. Not the British royal version, but one where she’s both the damsel and heroine, escaping the clutches of an evil institution to find her true calling. She wants to be something bigger, something uniquely American—royalty on her own terms, free from tradition but full of influence.

In Meghan’s world, she’s not the failed duchess but the woman who dared to rise above royal life. She’s self-anointed as the new face of American royalty. The trouble is, in America, royalty is fleeting. Yesterday’s queen is tomorrow’s tabloid fodder.

𝐀 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐰𝐨 𝐂𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐬

Ultimately, Meghan’s attempt to crown herself as America’s royalty may leave her stuck between two worlds. In Britain, her status is controversial; in America, she’s just another celebrity hoping for relevance in a crowded field. No title or PR stunt will cement her as true royalty in a land of Kardashians and Oprah Winfreys.

But don’t tell Meghan that. In her mind, she’s already America’s queen. Now, she just needs the world to agree. 
However, we find her staggering between disaster after disaster,  creating anything but a fairytale.

The fairy tale is over, and the clock has struck midnight for Meghan Markle. Once the dazzling darling of American celebrity culture, she now finds herself the subject of ridicule as the media turns against her with a vengeance. The creators of 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 recently unleashed a scathing episode that gleefully skewered the couple’s relentless quest for fame, poking fun at their so-called “Worldwide Privacy Tour.” In a delightful twist of irony, Meghan and Harry were portrayed as self-absorbed fame-seekers, proving that their desire for privacy is as sincere as a Hollywood starlet’s tearful confession on a talk show.

Fuel to this flaming dumpster of derision was thrown by none other than Bill Simmons, a 𝘚𝘱𝘰𝘵𝘪𝘧𝘺 executive, who infamously branded the Sussexes as “f***ing grifters” during a podcast. This blunt assessment reflects the mounting frustration within the industry over their much-hyped partnership, which ended with a whimper rather than a bang. The glow of admiration that once surrounded Meghan has dimmed to a flickering candlelight of exasperation, with outlets now dissecting the reality behind her royal façade and celebrity ambitions with a newly sharpened scalpel.

Adding insult to injury, 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘺𝘸𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘙𝘦𝘱𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘳 has not held back in its criticism. Commentator John McWhorter has dubbed Meghan “Duchess Difficult,” and “Dictator in Heels.” Such monikers perfectly encapsulate the desperate attempts by the Sussexes to reshape the royal narrative while profiting handsomely from their supposed victimhood. Once embraced by the Hollywood elite, Meghan now faces a chorus of eye rolls and side glances that echo the sentiment: “Not you again.”

The full extent of Meghan’s fall from grace was laid bare at the Los Angeles Children’s Hospital event, where reports emerged that she was asked to leave. Yes, the once-glittering star was ejected from a charity gala designed to help children in need—an event that should have been a soft landing for her in the world of philanthropy. Instead, it served as a glaring reminder that she has become persona non grata in the very circles that once admired her. When even a gala dinner aimed at children can’t tolerate your presence, it’s time to rethink your approach to celebrity.

AND NOW THIS LATEST FIASCO WITH THE COOKING SERIES!!


And yet, amid this American backlash, the British media continues to shower the Sussexes with the kind of affection usually reserved for long-lost royals. Why the disconnect? It’s a perplexing puzzle, considering the British tabloids have historically thrived on scandal and sensationalism. Perhaps the allure of a royal couple willing to spill family secrets and criticise the institution is just too tempting for them to resist, even as their American counterparts have grown weary of the spectacle.

One must wonder whether the British media is simply chasing clicks and profits or if they’ve confused their roles as royal correspondents for cheerleaders in a bizarre, never-ending pageant. After all, nothing sells like royal drama wrapped in celebrity glitter, and the Sussex saga is the gift that keeps on giving.

One can only marvel at their ability to ignore the growing disdain from across the pond while indulging in the latest scandal with enthusiasm. The question remains: are they genuinely invested in the royal family or merely opportunists ready to feast on the scraps of gossip that fall from the Sussexes’ table?

As the Sussex saga continues, it’s clear the royal couple now teeters on a precarious edge. The image they once sought to project is increasingly battered by a growing backlash. With the ground shifting rapidly beneath them, they may soon realise that the world they once tried to dominate has moved on, leaving them to navigate the fallout of their own making.

She seems to blunder from one thing to the next, a show in and of itself.

Rumours are rife that Prince Harry has taken a decisive step: filing for divorce from Meghan. The question on everyone’s lips, though, is where he’s done it. If he’s filed in the UK, it could potentially set a legal precedent around the custody of the couple’s two children. Given British jurisdiction’s potential role, the path to securing their future may not align with Meghan’s plans, and instead, could place them squarely within the traditions of the Royal Family.

The custody implications could be profound. Should the British courts have a say, it would open up avenues for the monarchy to reassert its influence over Harry’s children — a consideration given the historic British law on the guardianship of royal heirs. This law could prove advantageous for Harry if he wants to ensure the children maintain strong ties to the UK and the royal legacy they’ve been born into.

Beyond legalities, however, the rift between Harry and Meghan might expose Meghan’s public image to scrutiny from an angle she may not have anticipated. Harry is armed with knowledge that could counter any narrative Meghan spins in the memoir, she allegedly penning. He knows, as the British say, “where the bodies are buried.” If he were to publicly challenge the version of events she has cultivated, it could complicate her carefully managed image — and potentially cast doubt on her credibility.

If Harry were to return to the royal fold, it’s likely his role would echo that of another wayward royal, Prince Andrew. Seen, but not heard. Present but sidelined. The Royal Family, ever strategic, might just see value in such an arrangement — a quiet reclamation of one of their own that simultaneously disrupts Meghan’s media campaign. The subtle reabsorption of Harry would be a shrewd way to keep family matters from further public spectacle, shielding the monarchy’s image without fanfare.

Titles, of course, are more than mere formalities. Harry could voluntarily place his dukedom into abeyance, effectively removing Meghan’s right to use the Duchess of Sussex moniker, one she has wielded with financial acumen. Should their divorce be formalised, Meghan’s “Princess Henry of Wales” style — technically derived through marriage — could be withdrawn as well. Although it’s unlikely the King would ever grant Harry another dukedom, the division would mean that Meghan’s association with royalty would no longer hold the weight it once did, relegating her permanently outside the sphere of Windsor.

While much of this remains speculative, the legal and royal mechanisms are all in place. If Harry pursues this course, he could see his children’s ties to the UK strengthened, his titles strategically managed, and his own position within the royal fold restored, albeit quietly. This would mark the end of the Sussex chapter and the beginning of a new, redefined role for Harry — one that, even if understated, reinforces his place in the monarchy and keeps Meghan on the outside.

Isn’t it ironic that Prince Harry, who dove into marriage with reckless abandon, dares to critique the royal family’s choices in partners? In the first episode of the 2022 Netflix  Netflix mockumentary 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, he proclaimed that many men in the royal family are tempted to marry someone who “fits the mould” rather than someone they are truly destined to be with. Yet here he stands, the prime example of rushing into a marriage that seems more driven by lust than by genuine connection.    He should have asked their matchmaker " is she nice?"
a question she says she asked about him. 


While his father, King Charles III, and his brother, Prince William, took the time to cultivate genuine relationships based on mutual respect, Harry raced into a union with Meghan Markle, seemingly captivated by her allure and the thrill of rebellion rather than considering the qualities that truly matter in a lifelong partner. His eagerness to act on physical attraction has resulted in a marriage riddled with drama and uncertainty, a far cry from the stability his family has achieved with their chosen partners.

Harry’s self-righteous comments drip with hypocrisy. By disparaging his relatives, he inadvertently highlights his own failure to understand the weight of his choices. In criticising others for marrying out of obligation, he has shackled himself to a partner whose ambitions and quest for notoriety overshadow the very essence of partnership.

What Harry fails to grasp is that genuine love isn’t just about physical attraction; it requires patience, understanding, and the ability to weather life’s storms together. His criticisms fall flat against the backdrop of his own tumultuous marriage, which resembles a never-ending reality show more than a committed relationship.

Perhaps it would have been better if Harry had reflected on whether his own marital experience is the shining example of love he imagines it to be before casting stones from his glass house. In his attempt to rewrite the narrative of royal romance, he has instead penned a cautionary tale about the dangers of marrying without truly knowing the person beside him. As the drama continues to unfold, it becomes increasingly clear that Harry’s critiques only serve to magnify the missteps he has made on his own rocky road of ‘love’.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐱 𝐄𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐞: 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐨𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞, 𝐓𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝

In the latest chapter of the Sussexes’ post-palace saga, the power couple known for “escaping” the royal family’s golden cage seems to have run into a bit of a gilded problem of their own. Enter 𝘐𝘯𝘛𝘰𝘶𝘤𝘩’s newest headline: “𝘋𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘎𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘥!”—not exactly the fairy-tale ending they had in mind when they departed Britain’s shores, proclamations of independence trailing behind them.

Let’s dissect this “$100 million empire collapse,” shall we? For two people who once bemoaned the scrutiny and pressures of being in the royal fishbowl, Harry and Meghan sure seemed to make a swift U-turn back into the spotlight, albeit a more lucrative one. Who knew privacy could be so profitable? Between lucrative Netflix deals, star-studded Spotify podcasts, and tell-all book advances, they proved that fame can indeed be sold by the pound—until, it appears, the empire built on grievances and carefully crafted victimhood narratives began showing some cracks.

“𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘉𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴! screams the subhead, as if the world needed reminding of their extravagances. For Harry, the young prince who once dared to tell the world his father had financially abandoned him (while living in a multimillion-dollar Montecito mansion), financial reality may now be arriving with the grace of a stagecoach collision. As for Meghan, the transformation from a self-styled humanitarian to the Duchess of Dollar Signs has not exactly gone unnoticed.

And now, it seems, the “reckless royals” have reached the inevitable end of their fairy tale: not with the pomp and pageantry they once denounced, but with headlines about their “𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴!” Yes, the allure of billionaire ambitions was just too tantalising to resist, even for those who claimed to be fleeing the trappings of aristocratic privilege. One might say their undoing wasn’t so much greed as a relentless pursuit of relevance—wrapped in the velvet of luxury and sprinkled with a hint of delusion.

So, as the Sussex empire teeters, perhaps this isn’t the fairy tale they envisioned when they traded Buckingham Palace for a Californian castle. Instead of newfound freedom, it seems they’ve simply exchanged one gilded cage for another—only this time, the bars are forged by ambition, avarice, and a ravenous pursuit of fame.
As  they circle the proverbial drain,  at least it is a golden bit of plumbing that leads to the blue Pacific.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐫
One can almost hear the tumbleweed as Meghan Markle’s Hollywood dreams seem to be drifting off into the vast, arid Californian landscape. Once touted as the world’s most modern fairy tale—the American actress swept off her feet by a British prince—Meghan’s life now reads more like a comic book. The glamour has faded, the friends have vanished, and her fanbase has shrunk faster than a polyester dress in a hot wash.

Let’s be honest. Five years ago, when the Sussexes abandoned the royal fold, they were flooded with admiration and offers galore. Netflix inked an eye-watering nine-figure deal, and publishers threw themselves at their feet. Today? Well, you’d be forgiven for wondering if they’re keeping up with their own headlines. Meghan, a tragic cable TV actress, finds herself caught between the past and present attempts at glory—a stark reality for someone who fancied herself above royalty but is now facing a proper punch in the gut.

A recent onslaught of brutal critiques by Hollywood heavyweights has left the Duchess uncharacteristically quiet. Former Vanity Fair editor Tina Brown quipped that Meghan’s ideas were “total crap,” a remark that reflects a growing sentiment in an industry where image is everything and sympathy is an expense few are willing to invest in. Former allies in 𝘛𝘪𝘯𝘴𝘦𝘭𝘵𝘰𝘸𝘯—Oprah, Ellen, Serena—seem to be hiding behind their houseplants. Even her mega-agent, Ari Emanuel of the WME agency, hasn’t publicly lifted a finger, as the critiques continue piling up.  Oprah is so
ashamed of the interview that she did with the two of them she had it completely erased from the internet quite a while back. 
She should be ashamed to have show that horrible  "making fun of the curtsy moment"  that most likely pushed the queen over the edge. 


It’s fascinating, isn’t it? The woman who once marched through the British royal family like a hurricane, ‘revolutionising’ its supposed staid customs, now stands in the eye of a very different storm—one that’s colder, starker, and less forgiving. Hollywood Reporter dug up stories of terrified staff, Daily Beast resurrected tales of her “psycho moments” as a boss, and even former employees from her royal days have dared to pipe up, relishing the schadenfreude.

The Duchess has often argued that the British media is her biggest adversary, but the past few months suggest otherwise. Stories of Hollywood insiders recoiling and choosing to dodge the Markle brand are too numerous to brush off as tabloid vitriol. The whispers from these former friends of “absolutely relentless” behaviour and “marching around like a dictator in high heels” are now par for the course.

Adding to the bleak scene is the curious case of Meghan’s elusive lifestyle brand, ARO (American Riviera Orchard). Launched to much fanfare, it has since produced nothing but a solitary logo and was even slapped with a rejection from the U.S. Patent Office. Perhaps it was ambitious to assume that Meghan could charm the bureaucrats the same way she once charmed some with that toothy smile. But when one’s most talked-about business achievement is a stalled trademark application, it’s hard to claim the throne of entrepreneurship.

How ironic, too, that after all the Sussexes’ grand declarations about a new way forward, Meghan should now be remembered not for a semi-successful career, but for an old-school wannabe implosion. Oprah hasn’t leapt to her defence, Serena is silent, and Ellen, once so fond of her Montecito neighbour, has gone quiet as a late-night talk show on summer hiatus.

It seems that the Duchess’s star has waned, and that mighty agents and A-listers are seeing her for what she’s become: a once-shiny prospect now saddled with the baggage of failed ventures and burned bridges. Perhaps it’s time to face a hard truth. Meghan may well be the Duchess of Sussex, but in Hollywood? She’s becoming the Duchess of the Dollar.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞𝐬     Allow me a moment of reflection—a moment to thank South Park for saying, in blunt cartoon form, what we’ve all been thinking for far too long. It took a pair of animated misfits to finally unmask the Sussexes as the preening, privacy-loving paradoxes they are. And there they were: Harry, the wide-eyed prince who traded a crown for celebrity handshakes, and Meghan, the self-styled activist whose causes seem to end where the camera cuts. In one fell swoop, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 delivered what the world had been silently begging for: a full-throttle takedown of the Southparkles and their spectacular descent into self-parody.

Remember when these two high-tailed it out of Britain, bemoaning the shackles of royal life, only to shove their brand into every screen from Montecito to Manhattan? The escape to “freedom” quickly turned into a relentless self-promotional tour, complete with a glossy Netflix deal, weepy docu-series, and a Spotify podcast that droned on as vapidly as the platitudes they preach. Privacy, it turns out, is a state of mind—for the Sussexes, it’s one they scream about from every headline, podcast, and interview, their own echo chamber of self-pity.

𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 didn’t invent this farce; it merely held up a merciless mirror. They nailed Harry’s unearned martyrdom and Meghan’s shapeshifting causes, two perfectly polished caricatures of victimhood turned luxury brand. And what do the ‘Southparkles’ do in response? More finger-pointing, more grievances, another episode of “How the Palace Wronged Us,” as if the world hadn’t long ago tuned out. The Queen managed seventy years of scrutiny with grace, but two years of negative press have Harry and Meghan running to their lawyers—confirming that, yes, the only thing they’re actually good at is complaining.

In truth, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 gave them a rare gift: the one thing that’s been missing in the echo chamber of their own making—perspective. But, of course, Harry and Meghan can’t see the humour. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast: two people who desperately crave the spotlight, now reduced to cartoon characters in the cultural joke they can’t escape. Perhaps they should finally do us all a favour and give us the one thing they promised but never delivered—a quiet exit. Then again, where would the profit be in that?

Oh, the irony. Here we have the Duke and Duchess of Sussex—those self-styled champions of “privacy” who fled the royal fold to pursue their “authentic” lives—caught in the act of their true pursuit: piles upon piles of cash. Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? They only wanted privacy from the obligations, it seems—not from the cash and cameras that come with the royal titles they claim to despise.

If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

WE SEE YOU     ME GAIN,   AND IT IS NOT A GOOD LOOK.
