author: @mommapanda5736
text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐍𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐦

In a world that seems to worship the grandiose, few individuals exemplify the essence of narcissism quite like Meghan Markle. The erstwhile actress, now the Duchess of Sussex, has turned her life into a perpetual performance, and we are all unwilling spectators in her ongoing melodrama.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐰𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝𝐲: 𝐂𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬!

From the moment she entered the royal spotlight, Meghan made it clear she intended to be the headline act. The Oprah Winfrey interview was a masterclass in self-pity, shifting the focus from the monarchy to her own perceived suffering. It’s as if she believes her struggles warrant a Netflix series—a tawdry soap opera filled with tears and accusations.

𝐂𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐂𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐬: 𝐋𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞!

Meghan has transformed the media into her personal soapbox, scripting her narrative like a desperate writer. She unleashes well-timed leaks to cast herself as the misunderstood outsider battling an archaic institution. Instead of rising to the occasion during royal turmoil, Meghan threw a tantrum on international television, crafting an image so far removed from reality it resembles fantasy.

𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐬? 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐈𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞!

In Meghan’s world, relationships are expendable. Her estrangement from her father and half-siblings reads like a bad drama. She keeps only those who serve her narrative, including her infamous rift with the royal family—an institution she clearly disdains. If she isn’t the centre of attention, she seems to lose interest, leaving a trail of broken connections.

𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠

Meghan’s relentless pursuit of fame is astounding. She traded royal duties for Hollywood deals faster than you can say “publicity stunt,” signing multi-million-pound contracts while lamenting her loss of privacy. Does she care for philanthropy, or is her true love the fleeting high of applause?

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐎𝐥𝐲𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐬: 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐏𝐢𝐭𝐲

While advocating for social issues, Meghan’s approach often feels like a marketing strategy rather than genuine concern. Each speech draws more attention to her trauma than the causes she claims to support. It’s hard to take seriously a woman who has lived in palaces while positioning herself as a martyr, using her platform for personal grievances rather than the greater good.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 — 𝐀 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐆𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐠𝐞

Meghan Markle serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of narcissism. In her quest for independence and recognition, she has alienated herself from those who might offer her support. It begs the question: in a world filled with adoration and applause, will she ever find the genuine connections she seems so desperately to seek? For all her talk of freedom and authenticity, Meghan remains trapped in a gilded cage of her own making, where the pursuit of fame ultimately leaves her more isolated than ever.

And while the world watches her every move, one thing is certain: Meghan Markle is the star of her own show, and it’s a performance that reveals far more about her character than she would like to admit.

𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐀 𝐅𝐢𝐬𝐡 𝐎𝐮𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫

What happens when a prince swaps palaces for podcasts, duty for documentaries, and centuries of tradition for Californian sunsets? In the curious case of Prince Harry, it’s a tale of a man who bolted from the confines of royalty only to find himself stranded in a sea of contradictions, floundering like a fish out of royal water.

Remember Harry? The cheeky royal who once charmed us with his wild antics, his rogueish grin, and his unmistakable aura of second-born freedom? Well, that Harry seems to have taken a wrong turn somewhere between Windsor Castle and Montecito. These days, he’s less the dashing Duke of Sussex and more the poster child for disillusionment—permanently aggrieved, perpetually misunderstood, and endlessly cashing in on his own victimhood.

When he left the royal family in 2020, we were told it was for the sake of privacy and peace. Yet here we are, four years later, and there’s been little of either. Privacy? It seems Harry and Meghan can’t stop broadcasting every grievance, every slight, every festering family issue to the world via Netflix, Spotify, and Oprah. Peace? Hardly. The Prince has seemingly turned complaining into a full-time job, with his memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 and endless media appearances keeping the family drama firmly in the public eye.

In this new Californian life, Harry looks painfully out of place. He once stood shoulder to shoulder with global leaders, soldiers, and the British public. Now, he spends his days hobnobbing with Hollywood's elite, surrounded by sycophants and Netflix producers who lap up his every tale of woe. The problem? He’s not a Hollywood star, no matter how much he tries to play the part. He’s the royal who ditched the Crown, but still can’t seem to let go of its shine.

What’s most baffling is that the very thing Harry claims to despise—his royal status—is the same thing he’s used to fuel his new life. Strip away the titles and what remains? It’s not Harry, the ordinary man, the loving husband, or the mental health advocate that draws the millions. No, it’s Prince Harry, son of Princess Diana, brother of the future king, estranged grandson of the late Queen. Without the monarchy, without the endless royal drama, the Sussexes’ appeal shrinks faster than Harry’s hairline.

And while Harry flounders in his quest for a meaningful identity beyond "the spare," the irony is laid bare. In leaving the royal family to escape being defined by it, he has never been more defined by it. His every utterance, every appearance is laced with royal references, always circling back to the same tired grievances against The Firm. He loathes the monarchy, yet he cannot seem to stop talking about it.

He’s a fish out of royal water, all right—a royal who traded his birthright for the promise of freedom and a Californian dream. But instead of swimming into the sunset, he’s floundering in the shallow end, trapped by the very fame he wanted to escape. 

Meanwhile, as his Netflix deals wane and the public grows weary of the endless tales of betrayal, one wonders how long Harry can keep playing the victim card. His status as the poor prince wronged by the system has a shelf life, and it’s rapidly approaching its expiration date. For a man who has always seemed more at home in combat gear than cashmere sweaters, it’s hard to imagine him truly fitting into this celebrity world long term.

But perhaps that’s the tragedy of Prince Harry: a man who once had it all but chose to walk away, only to find out that life beyond the palace gates isn't all it's cracked up to be. The fish may have leapt out of the royal pond, but it seems he’s struggling to breathe in his new, self-made ocean of irrelevance.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞𝐬 

Allow me a moment of reflection—a moment to thank South Park for saying, in blunt cartoon form, what we’ve all been thinking for far too long. It took a pair of animated misfits to finally unmask the Sussexes as the preening, privacy-loving paradoxes they are. And there they were: Harry, the wide-eyed prince who traded a crown for celebrity handshakes, and Meghan, the self-styled activist whose causes seem to end where the camera cuts. In one fell swoop, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 delivered what the world had been silently begging for: a full-throttle takedown of the Southparkles and their spectacular descent into self-parody.

Remember when these two high-tailed it out of Britain, bemoaning the shackles of royal life, only to shove their brand into every screen from Montecito to Manhattan? The escape to “freedom” quickly turned into a relentless self-promotional tour, complete with a glossy Netflix deal, weepy docu-series, and a Spotify podcast that droned on as vapidly as the platitudes they preach. Privacy, it turns out, is a state of mind—for the Sussexes, it’s one they scream about from every headline, podcast, and interview, their own echo chamber of self-pity.

𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 didn’t invent this farce; it merely held up a merciless mirror. They nailed Harry’s unearned martyrdom and Meghan’s shapeshifting causes, two perfectly polished caricatures of victimhood turned luxury brand. And what do the ‘Southparkles’ do in response? More finger-pointing, more grievances, another episode of “How the Palace Wronged Us,” as if the world hadn’t long ago tuned out. The Queen managed seventy years of scrutiny with grace, but two years of negative press have Harry and Meghan running to their lawyers—confirming that, yes, the only thing they’re actually good at is complaining.

In truth, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 gave them a rare gift: the one thing that’s been missing in the echo chamber of their own making—perspective. But, of course, Harry and Meghan can’t see the humour. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast: two people who desperately crave the spotlight, now reduced to cartoon characters in the cultural joke they can’t escape. Perhaps they should finally do us all a favour and give us the one thing they promised but never delivered—a quiet exit. Then again, where would the profit be in that?

text:
𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

Maybe netflix can go back to the kitchen and start over.

text:
𝐀 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐓𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐢𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬

If we were to transpose Prince Harry’s behaviour to the time of our ancestors, the boy would find himself not in the opulent halls of a palace but rather in the dank confines of the Tower of London, languishing in chains. For in a bygone age, when treachery was dealt with by more than just the dubious appeasement of public opinion, he would have been dispatched to the tower quicker than you can say ‘traitor.’

Imagine the scene: a raucous court, gossip swirling like smoke from a Tudor fireplace. The nobles, their heads adorned with plumed hats, would shake their heads in disbelief, horrified at Harry’s audacity. This is a man who has squandered his royal birthright on a flimsy narrative of self-pity and the incessant drone of ‘me, me, me.’ Once the darling of the nation, he has plunged from grace faster than one of his cringe-inducing lectures.

The Tower, with its grim history of imprisoning those who dared to defy the crown, would be a fitting abode for our runaway prince. Here, amidst the echo of clanking chains and the occasional crow of a raven perched on the battlements, he would reflect on his many misdeeds—turning his back on a family steeped in tradition and duty. It is no exaggeration to say that he has become a masterclass in public disgrace, with a Netflix contract in hand and a penchant for revealing family secrets like a particularly scandalous Victorian novel.

Let us not forget the allies he has chosen—his wife, who seems intent on making headlines as though they were some sort of royalty-obsessed Kardashians, and a media machine that churns out sympathy pieces like a factory line of self-serving narratives. In the days of yore, such behaviour would have led to a one-way ticket to the Tower, where the only entertainment would be the occasional visit from the executioner, brandishing his axe with the same disdain the British public now holds for the Sussexes.

And who could blame us? Harry’s relentless parade of grievances—his childhood traumas, his estranged family, his perpetual victimhood—has grown tiresome. It feels as if he has taken the lessons of his late mother, Princess Diana, and turned them into a sordid reality show, where every episode is marked by betrayal and an insatiable need for public approval. One might argue that Diana, had she been around, would have given him a stern talking-to, perhaps even a ‘get a grip, Harry’ lecture over a cup of tea.

As he and Meghan traipse around the globe, preaching the virtues of mental health while simultaneously making a mockery of their own familial ties, one can’t help but wonder if their antics might prompt a royal edict—‘Let them eat cake’ as they sit in their ivory tower, oblivious to the discontent brewing below. For in this land of pomp and pageantry, where tradition is revered, their antics are as out of place as a jester in a cathedral.

Ultimately, Harry won’t find himself in the Tower, but perhaps it’s time to ponder the legacy he is crafting for himself—one of disgrace rather than distinction. In a world that once revered him, he now stands as a cautionary tale, a prince turned pauper of public opinion. It’s a royal disgrace that would make any self-respecting Prince shudder in their boots. If only he could hear the whispers of history echoing through the stone walls, reminding him that treachery, once committed, has a way of finding its just desserts.

text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

author: @mommapanda5736
text:
What is the   ARCHEWELL FOUNDATION    Vanity project or Laundering scheme???

The Archewell Foundation’s so-called mission to create “positive change around the world” is a masterclass in vagueness, empty promises, and headline-grabbing PR moves that amount to little more than a glorified vanity project for Meghan Markle and Harry. When you peel back the buzzwords and jargon, it becomes glaringly obvious: Archewell is more about elevating their brand than helping the vulnerable. 


Let’s begin with the staff—if you can even keep track of them. The Archewell Foundation has become notorious for its revolving door of executives and key employees. James Holt, Catherine St. Laurent, Richard Genow, and Andrew Meyer—none lasted long, with most leaving after short stints working what amounts to one-hour work weeks on paper. With high-profile names constantly jumping ship, the question arises: why can’t they retain top talent? The constant exodus speaks volumes about the chaotic mismanagement within the organization. 

And let’s not forget their notorious “pledge” debacle. Much like Amber Heard’s infamous courtroom moment where she conflated a ‘pledge’ with an actual donation, Harry and Meghan seem to have adopted the same creative accounting. They throw around promises of grand initiatives and charitable contributions, but the follow-through? Practically non-existent. Announcing lofty donations and then conveniently failing to provide any real evidence of these funds reaching those in need has become their modus operandi. Where’s the accountability? 

Their recent trip to Colombia to 'empower' youth with the “transformative power of arts and dance” is another perfect example of their smoke-and-mirrors philanthropy. Buzzwords like ‘amplification’ and ‘equitable impact’ are great for press releases, but where are the concrete results? Handing out a few drums and calling it a day is hardly the world-changing impact they claim to have. No measurable outcomes, no real commitment—just another PR stunt to make headlines and keep their brand relevant.

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐎𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐡 𝐓𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐫𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐚𝐜𝐞-𝐁𝐚𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠?

Prince Harry may have thought he was marrying a modern fairy tale princess, but in reality, he snagged a master of manipulation in Meghan Markle. Ever since her explosive interview with Oprah Winfrey, where she alleged that the royal family had concerns about the skin tone of her son, Meghan has turned the narrative of her life into a dramatic race-filled saga.

Oprah, the queen of emotional storytelling, provided the perfect platform for Meghan to air her grievances, and Meghan seized it with both hands. Who could forget the way Oprah nodded sympathetically as Meghan unleashed a torrent of allegations against the monarchy, turning the institution into a villainous caricature? In that moment, the duchess became a victim, not just of royal protocols but of an insidious racism that allegedly permeated the family.

But here’s the rub: Meghan’s claims have often seemed more about personal branding than genuine advocacy. With her penchant for race-baiting, she seems to wield racial identity like a badge of honour, playing the victim card to garner sympathy and elevate her status. Critics argue that she has turned serious issues into fodder for a personal narrative, expertly blurring the line between empowerment and exploitation.

As Meghan continues to spin her story, one must wonder: did Oprah’s influence teach her that a well-placed accusation can overshadow all else? In the game of celebrity, race is the ultimate trump card, and Meghan has learned to play it with a finesse that would make even the most seasoned media mogul envious.

As the saga continues to unfold, we’re left to ponder whether Meghan Markle is simply a savvy storyteller or just someone who knows how to play the race card to her advantage.

text:
𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞: 𝐀 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞'𝐬 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐝𝐲

In the grand tapestry of royal narratives, Prince Harry's journey resembles a Shakespearean tragedy infused with farce. Born into privilege, his life has morphed into a soap opera, largely due to his union with Meghan Markle.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐬

Before Meghan, Harry was the affable spare—beloved for his military service and the Invictus Games. Enter Meghan, and suddenly, Harry's life becomes a whirlwind of controversies. From stepping back as a senior royal to transatlantic drama, this prince seems to prefer the spotlight over tradition.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐦 𝐒𝐮𝐦𝐦𝐢𝐭: 𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

The Sandringham Summit in January 2020 exemplifies a turning point in Harry’s story. In a rare display of unity, Queen Elizabeth, Prince Charles, and Prince William urged him to reconsider his choices and the implications for the monarchy. Rather than taking this moment for reflection and healing family rifts, Harry’s steadfast resolve to diverge from royal traditions became evident. He drew a line in the sand, setting the stage for his departure into celebrity and closing the door on a life steeped in duty and heritage. In doing so, he not only severed ties with the expectations of his royal role but also embarked on a path that would redefine his identity outside the monarchy, leaving behind a legacy of unfulfilled potential and fractured family bonds.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐦

Harry's issues escalated dramatically after marrying Meghan. Was it the allure of American celebrity culture that caused this? Or was it Meghan's Hollywood background that catalysed his royal meltdown? What began as a love story turned into a narrative where every decision seemed calculated to stir public opinion.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

The couple's move to the US, ostensibly for privacy, has instead become a masterclass in courting controversy while claiming victimhood. From their infamous interview with Oprah Winfrey to a Netflix series depicting their royal life as a sitcom, Harry's existence has devolved into a spectacle of grievances.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞’𝐬 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐑𝐨𝐥𝐞

Harry's transformation from a promising royal to a polarising figure appears largely driven by Meghan. However, this narrative often overlooks his agency; he confirmed their relationship to fend off scrutiny, only to be ensnared in drama of his own making. Despite being given a year to reassess his life after stepping down, he remains entrenched in chaos.

𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐈𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Public sentiment oscillates between sympathy for Harry's plight and derision over his self-imposed isolation. He has become a cautionary tale—a man who traded royal duty for celebrity antics, alienating himself from the institution that once defined him. His narrative is now one of self-inflicted chaos rather than service.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞'𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚

Ultimately, Prince Harry's story may not be remembered for his charm but for the chaos following Meghan's entrance. What began as typical spare troubles have evolved into a cautionary tale of a prince lost in a narrative he embraced. Whether his chapter in royal history will be viewed as a misguided love story or a reflection of ambition and controversy remains to be seen. For now, Harry’s fall from grace is irrevocably tied to his marriage.

The royal spotlight has turned into a funhouse mirror, reflecting not a dashing prince but a figure ensnared in the tragicomedy of his life. “Forever the spare, forever the spectacle.”

text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤… 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐨𝐭𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle once declared their intention to step back from royal life, seeking a quieter existence away from the relentless media scrutiny, the invasive headlines, and the unending circus of royal duty. We all remember that moment in January 2020 when the world collectively gasped at their decision to break free from the gilded cage of monarchy. They wanted, they said, to live in peace. They craved privacy.

But fast forward to today, and one has to wonder—if privacy was truly the goal, why do Harry and Meghan constantly seek out the spotlight like moths to a flame? After all, we’ve hardly been short of the couple these past few years, have we? And every time we think they’re retreating into the shadows, back they come, brighter than ever, ready to tell us more, reveal more, and sell more.

𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐃𝐮𝐭𝐲 𝐭𝐨 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐟𝐥𝐢𝐱 𝐃𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬

When Harry and Meghan announced their “progressive new role” in early 2020, they claimed they would split their time between the UK and North America, free from the relentless scrutiny of the British press. They wanted to raise their children away from prying eyes, to live like regular people.

Well, if this is what regular people do—signing £100 million deals with Netflix—then sign me up! Because just months after their grand exit from royal life, the couple inked a lucrative contract with the streaming giant to produce documentaries, films, and television shows. Their docuseries, 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 & 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧, provided intimate glimpses of their lives—precisely the kind of exposure they once claimed to flee from.

One can only marvel at the paradox: “Please leave us alone,” they plead, while flinging open the doors to their California mansion, cameras rolling, lights flashing.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐡 𝐁𝐨𝐦𝐛𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐥

Ah, but we’re not done. Who can forget 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 interview with Oprah Winfrey in March 2021? Broadcast to millions across the globe, Harry and Meghan laid bare their grievances with the royal family in what was undoubtedly the most talked-about television moment of the year. Harry lamented the toxic tabloid culture that hounded them, but in the next breath, the couple dropped bombshell after bombshell that sent those very tabloids into a feeding frenzy.

Was this stepping away from the limelight? Hardly. This was stepping right into the fire—voluntarily.

 ‘𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞’ 𝐔𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐚

As if the Oprah interview wasn’t enough, along came *Spare*, Harry’s tell-all memoir published in early 2023. Within its pages, Harry spilled secrets from the very heart of royal life—recollections of private conversations, moments of familial tension, and, oh yes, that infamous fight with his brother William. The book broke sales records but also shattered any remaining illusion that Harry and Meghan desired a quiet life. They weren’t running from the spotlight; they were standing squarely in its centre, microphone in hand, demanding more.

To promote ‘𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞’ Harry and Meghan embarked on a media blitz, appearing on television interviews, podcasts, and talk shows—each one more revealing than the last. Privacy? This isn’t privacy. This is public relations, plain and simple.

All the wanted was  𝐀 𝐃𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐊𝐢𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞.

As Meghan continues to spin her story, one must wonder: did Oprah’s influence teach her that a well-placed accusation can overshadow all else? In the game of celebrity, race is the ultimate trump card, and Meghan has learned to play it with a finesse that would make even the most seasoned media mogul envious.

As the saga continues to unfold, we’re left to ponder whether Meghan Markle is simply a savvy storyteller or just someone who knows how to play the race card to her advantage.

𝟕𝟐 𝐇𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐲𝐫𝐝𝐨𝐦: 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞’𝐬 𝐌𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐢𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐲

Oh, the irony! Meghan Markle, our ‘favourite’ Duchess of Dismay, is reportedly working on a tell-all memoir about her alleged 72 hours as a working royal. Yes, that’s right—three days in a tiara, and she’s convinced she has enough material to rival Shakespeare’s tragedies. I can hardly wait for the enlightening tales of adversity that surely await us. Spoiler alert: I suspect they’ll be as riveting as watching paint dry.

Let’s not forget that Meghan’s grand total of royal duties could hardly fill a pamphlet, yet she’s poised to regale us with her experiences as if she survived a shipwreck. In those fleeting 72 hours, she managed to squeeze in a handful of engagements before she and Harry were off, leaving behind a trail of baffled courtiers and one very confused corgi. But alas, this is the same woman who turned a mere two years in the spotlight into an epic saga of betrayal and emotional trauma. So why stop now?

What can we expect from this memoir? A deep dive into the horrors of royal life? A gripping narrative detailing the systemic oppression she faced from her fellow royals? I can only imagine the subheadings: “Chapter One: The Cruelty of Curtsying” and “Chapter Two: The Unbearable Weight of the Crown.” Truly, who knew tiaras could be so oppressive?

If her previous forays into storytelling are anything to go by, we can anticipate another round of victimhood, complete with dramatic retellings of her time in the palace. Perhaps she’ll recount the agonising moment when she discovered the palace didn’t come with a personal stylist or how she was forced to endure the trials of royal protocol while trying to navigate a world where she was expected to smile and wave.

But let’s be real. This memoir is destined to be another whinge-fest, a victim’s manifesto penned by a woman who spent more time on Instagram than she did attending royal events. Meghan will undoubtedly fill the pages with tales of how she was misunderstood, how her mental health was allegedly jeopardised by the stuffy traditions of the monarchy, and how she was forced to endure life with “difficult” people like the Queen and Prince Charles.

And of course, no memoir of hers would be complete without the obligatory accusations of racism and systemic cruelty. It’s the get out of jail free card in her narrative, allowing her to play the role of the wronged princess in a fairytale gone horribly awry. Who knew a three-day stint could come with so many grievances?

In the end, Meghan’s memoir will likely reflect more on her relentless quest for victimhood than any real insights into the workings of the royal family. If she really believes she can turn a brief royal experience into a bestseller, then bless her heart. I’d wager my hat that it’ll be yet another saga of self-pity dressed up as profound wisdom.

So, fasten your seatbelts, Meghan Markle is about to take us on yet another wild ride through her self-crafted narrative, and I have a feeling it’s going to be one heck of a predictable journey!

text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐞'𝐬 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚'𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐧

Meghan Markle, self-styled "duchess of the people," seems to have quietly elevated herself to the role of America’s queen. No tiaras, no palaces (unless Montecito counts), and no coronation. Instead, she’s created her own version of royalty, blending celebrity and titles with a hefty Netflix deal. In her mind, she’s not just part of a royal family; she is *the* royal family.

This didn’t happen overnight. From the moment she walked down the aisle at St George’s Chapel, Meghan appeared more Hollywood than Windsor. That twinkle wasn’t the glow of a new duchess embracing regal duty—it was the gleam of someone who had just landed the lead role in a global drama. But a supporting role wasn’t enough. Meghan had bigger dreams.

From the outset, she crafted herself as the archetype of modern royalty—glamorous, relatable (if you like $14 million mansions), and oppressed by a world that "didn’t understand her." Meghan isn’t interested in the pomp of Old Blighty; she craves adulation, magazine covers, and the constant spotlight. Her royalty is less about duty and more about celebrity.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭 𝐄𝐬𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞

When Meghan and Harry left royal life for California, many thought they sought peace. Instead, they reinvented themselves as America’s answer to royalty. Setting up a multimillion-dollar media empire, they seemed to cast themselves as the new royal family of the West Coast. Meghan, especially, embraced her role as America’s princess—wronged by an archaic institution, now "finding her voice" in the land of the free.

But America already has its own royalty—Hollywood. It doesn’t follow Windsor rules; it’s ruthless, fickle, and loves a scandal more than a curated PR image. Meghan, like an ingénue, believes she can be both a Hollywood queen and a royal duchess. The trouble is, she’s not quite pulling it off.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧

Despite claiming to seek a "normal" life, Meghan clings to her royal title like a last Louis Vuitton bag on Rodeo Drive. In every appearance, she’s “the Duchess of Sussex.” Her role in American life is drenched in royal overtones—co-founding Archewell, lecturing from her Montecito mansion, and wielding her title like a sceptre.

Meghan forgets that in America, titles don’t make you royal. What works in the UK, where centuries of tradition cushion you, doesn’t fly across the Atlantic. Here, you’re only as royal as your last deal. Americans love their celebrities messy and flawed, not preachy.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐖𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐬

Meghan is obsessed with her own fairytale. Not the British royal version, but one where she’s both the damsel and heroine, escaping the clutches of an evil institution to find her true calling. She wants to be something bigger, something uniquely American—royalty on her own terms, free from tradition but full of influence.

In Meghan’s world, she’s not the failed duchess but the woman who dared to rise above royal life. She’s self-anointed as the new face of American royalty. The trouble is, in America, royalty is fleeting. Yesterday’s queen is tomorrow’s tabloid fodder.

𝐀 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐰𝐨 𝐂𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐬

Ultimately, Meghan’s attempt to crown herself as America’s royalty may leave her stuck between two worlds. In Britain, her status is controversial; in America, she’s just another celebrity hoping for relevance in a crowded field. No title or PR stunt will cement her as true royalty in a land of Kardashians and Oprah Winfreys.

But don’t tell Meghan that. In her mind, she’s already America’s queen. Now, she just needs the world to agree.

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞𝐬 

Allow me a moment of reflection—a moment to thank South Park for saying, in blunt cartoon form, what we’ve all been thinking for far too long. It took a pair of animated misfits to finally unmask the Sussexes as the preening, privacy-loving paradoxes they are. And there they were: Harry, the wide-eyed prince who traded a crown for celebrity handshakes, and Meghan, the self-styled activist whose causes seem to end where the camera cuts. In one fell swoop, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 delivered what the world had been silently begging for: a full-throttle takedown of the Southparkles and their spectacular descent into self-parody.

Remember when these two high-tailed it out of Britain, bemoaning the shackles of royal life, only to shove their brand into every screen from Montecito to Manhattan? The escape to “freedom” quickly turned into a relentless self-promotional tour, complete with a glossy Netflix deal, weepy docu-series, and a Spotify podcast that droned on as vapidly as the platitudes they preach. Privacy, it turns out, is a state of mind—for the Sussexes, it’s one they scream about from every headline, podcast, and interview, their own echo chamber of self-pity.

𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 didn’t invent this farce; it merely held up a merciless mirror. They nailed Harry’s unearned martyrdom and Meghan’s shapeshifting causes, two perfectly polished caricatures of victimhood turned luxury brand. And what do the ‘Southparkles’ do in response? More finger-pointing, more grievances, another episode of “How the Palace Wronged Us,” as if the world hadn’t long ago tuned out. The Queen managed seventy years of scrutiny with grace, but two years of negative press have Harry and Meghan running to their lawyers—confirming that, yes, the only thing they’re actually good at is complaining.

In truth, 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 gave them a rare gift: the one thing that’s been missing in the echo chamber of their own making—perspective. But, of course, Harry and Meghan can’t see the humour. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast: two people who desperately crave the spotlight, now reduced to cartoon characters in the cultural joke they can’t escape. Perhaps they should finally do us all a favour and give us the one thing they promised but never delivered—a quiet exit. Then again, where would the profit be in that?

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

text: I’m not one to typically comment, and don’t know meghan markle so certainly cannot comment on her character. What I do feel compelled to express is that this trailer really conveys a very tone def and confusing image. 1:00  ‘We’re not in the pursuit of perfection, we’re in the pursuit of joy’ whilst every shot depicts carefully curated scenes of beautiful perfectly cut cake, perfectly bloomed flowers, perfectly manicured nails, makeup and hair, is regrettably lacking in insight and forces me (and likely others) to feel put off and like she cannot be trusted. It conveys the message ‘my biggest fault is that I am too perfect, I can’t help being good at everything’, and at best reveals deep insecurity and at worse grandiosity that so often accompanies that sentiment. Implicit in such a perspective (even if unintentional) is that ‘I am better than you’. Meghan Markle is human, and probably a loving partner and mother, insecurity is natural, she has good taste and it’s sad she cannot create without being ridiculed and mocked. But it is sad if after all she has been through she cannot recognise that. Moreover, if Netflix cared about their cashcows they should have encouraged a far more raw expression of that insecurity without the contrived and controlled cinematography that has seeped into all of their documentaries. It’s sad really.

author: @ocdman202
text:
OPEN LETTER TO HARRY:

Hi Harry. . You suffered a childhood trauma when you lost your mother and I also suffered a similar trauma when I lost my father in those very difficult ages between 9-12. What you suffered next was the neglect of a rich parent. I suffered the neglect of an impoverished parent. What I've learned from this book is that it was neglect all the same. I'm telling you this very personal thing because I am older than you and I am seeing the very painful path that you are on. Consider this one idea for a course correction.

1. Forgive your Pa, Harry. For everything. His neglect. His inability to parent. His marriage to Camilla - the love of his life. Forgive him even if he is guilty of planting items in the press for his own good. It is clear you have a Pa size hole in your heart and I bet your Pa has a similar sized hole in his heart. Be the bridge. Do not be the fire. Fire is death and destruction. Your most intimate stories in this book tell of a man - you - that is gentle and loving.

2. Yep - forgive Willy and Kate. Willy also had trauma. He is handling it differently than you. Nonetheless he must also handle it in his own way. You must give him permission to do this because you also are doing that. Hop on a commercial plane with Archie. Bring him to Balmoral or wherever you all hang out now. Leave Meghan at home - just for now. Build your relationship with your brother through your children. Forgive him and erase those dang texts that you are saving with angry words. Never keep angry words stored by people that you love. You will never be able to get over those words if you re-read them. Just meet Willy where he is at and stop demanding an immediate fix to a problem that both of you hold blame for. Put down the swords. When you are in your 50s and 60s it may well be too late to solve these problems. Tackle them now. There is a Harold sized hole in his heart. You can fill it.

3. Do not force a relationship between Kate and Meghan. That would be ridiculous. The bridesmaid dresses, the lip gloss is all water under the bridge. Kate has not been raised "American" and Meghan should not treat her as such. If a relationship is to be built, it will be long after you re-establish a relationship with your brother. Meghan is on her own with Kate.

4. Last - get over this crud about being the SPARE. This is the most ridiculous title for your memoir. You are "cutting yourself" over and over with this title and this thought. How about if you consider yourself SPARE-D?? By God, Harry, you have been given the great, great gift of freedom that your brother will never experience. Live your freedom and rejoice in it. Go earn a living and love those children and wife with everything you have. This is your gift. Do not give it back like a spoiled child.

5. I think, ultimately, if you can find a way to make yourself as small as possible in this world and just observe you will see what I am talking about. Right now, your face is taking up the whole screen and you are too big in your own head. For example, other than you bringing it up again in this book, no one was really going to remember the strip poker in Las Vegas or needed to know about your frozen penis or so many other examples when you have felt too large for the world. The collective memory is really rather small and you just need to let it fade.

6. You need to up your coping skills. You are allowing yourself to be too fragile. Learn to cope with the life you have been given - all of it.

text:
𝐈'𝐦 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝": 𝐀 𝐌𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐇𝐲𝐩𝐨𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐲

Here we go again. Someone who has spent a lifetime wielding their privilege like a weapon now claims to be the “most bullied person in the world.” Spare us the theatrics. Perhaps if you had treated everyone you encountered—friends, family, and the unsuspecting public—with a smidge of kindness and humility, the global reaction might have been a tad more favourable. 

But no, instead you’ve opted for a personal brand of destruction that insults friends and family alike, emotionally abuses the elderly, and allegedly blackmails the royal family. If there’s a litany of bad behaviour that screams “victim,” yours is it. The entitlement you displayed when demanding to move into Windsor Castle or expecting the Australian Prime Minister to vacate his residence for your convenience is nothing short of staggering. The cheek! And let’s not even get started on your derisive comments about the accommodations provided by South African ministers during your jaunt there—how charming.

You’ve curated an online cult of cruelty that would make the worst schoolyard bully blush. Instead of fostering compassion, you’ve encouraged a toxic atmosphere of hate and ridicule, hounding your detractors with vicious, derogatory comments. It’s baffling how someone can be so ungracious while playing the victim card so shamelessly.

Then, there’s your cold dismissal treatment of your elderly father and siblings, an act so shockingly cruel it would make even the most hardened cynics wince. This pattern of rudeness, ingratitude, and self-aggrandisement is precisely why you’re met with derision and disdain. Yet, instead of taking a good hard look in the mirror and accepting responsibility, you deflect blame like a master escape artist.

Let’s cut to the chase: you are the architect of your own downfall. It’s time to put away the crocodile tears and stop the pity party. A true path to redemption requires humility, self-reflection, and a genuine apology to those you’ve wronged. But let’s be real—do you have it in you to transform from a self-styled diva into something resembling a decent human being? I doubt it. Even if you tried, the public would be hard-pressed to take you seriously. 

True change comes from acknowledging one’s flaws and making amends. Until you can do that, this tiresome narrative of victimhood will continue to ring hollow. You’ve played the part of the wronged party for too long, and it’s getting increasingly difficult to believe that the world is at fault for your woes. Look around—maybe, just maybe, the issue lies with you. MEGHAN...

text:
𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐍𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐦

In a world that seems to worship the grandiose, few individuals exemplify the essence of narcissism quite like Meghan Markle. The erstwhile actress, now the Duchess of Sussex, has turned her life into a perpetual performance, and we are all unwilling spectators in her ongoing melodrama.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐰𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝𝐲: 𝐂𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬!

From the moment she entered the royal spotlight, Meghan made it clear she intended to be the headline act. The Oprah Winfrey interview was a masterclass in self-pity, shifting the focus from the monarchy to her own perceived suffering. It’s as if she believes her struggles warrant a Netflix series—a tawdry soap opera filled with tears and accusations.

She keeps only those who serve her narrative, including her infamous rift with the royal family—an institution she clearly disdains. text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

Yes, that’s right—three days in a tiara, and she’s convinced she has enough material to rival Shakespeare’s tragedies. I can hardly wait for the enlightening tales of adversity that surely await us. Spoiler alert: I suspect they’ll be as riveting as watching paint dry.

Let’s not forget that Meghan’s grand total of royal duties could hardly fill a pamphlet, yet she’s poised to regale us with her experiences as if she survived a shipwreck. In those fleeting 72 hours, she managed to squeeze in a handful of engagements before she and Harry were off, leaving behind a trail of baffled courtiers and one very confused corgi. But alas, this is the same woman who turned a mere two years in the spotlight into an epic saga of betrayal and emotional trauma. So why stop now?

What can we expect from this memoir? A deep dive into the horrors of royal life? A gripping narrative detailing the systemic oppression she faced from her fellow royals? I can only imagine the subheadings: “Chapter One: The Cruelty of Curtsying” and “Chapter Two: The Unbearable Weight of the Crown.” Truly, who knew tiaras could be so oppressive?

If her previous forays into storytelling are anything to go by, we can anticipate another round of victimhood, complete with dramatic retellings of her time in the palace. Perhaps she’ll recount the agonising moment when she discovered the palace didn’t come with a personal stylist or how she was forced to endure the trials of royal protocol while trying to navigate a world where she was expected to smile and wave.

But let’s be real. This memoir is destined to be another whinge-fest, a victim’s manifesto penned by a woman who spent more time on Instagram than she did attending royal events. Meghan will undoubtedly fill the pages with tales of how she was misunderstood, how her mental health was allegedly jeopardised by the stuffy traditions of the monarchy, and how she was forced to endure life with “difficult” people like the Queen and Prince Charles.

And of course, no memoir of hers would be complete without the obligatory accusations of racism and systemic cruelty. It’s the get out of jail free card in her narrative, allowing her to play the role of the wronged princess in a fairytale gone horribly awry. Who knew a three-day stint could come with so many grievances?

In the end, Meghan’s memoir will likely reflect more on her relentless quest for victimhood than any real insights into the workings of the royal family. If she really believes she can turn a brief royal experience into a bestseller, then bless her heart. I’d wager my hat that it’ll be yet another saga of self-pity dressed up as profound wisdom.

So, fasten your seatbelts, Meghan Markle is about to take us on yet another wild ride through her self-crafted narrative, and I have a feeling it’s going to be one heck of a predictable journey!

He’d been through it all: polo matches, helicopter rescues, the occasional scandal involving a Las Vegas hotel room. And then, along came the beautiful American actress, who swept him off his feet and promised a life of freedom, love, and media deals. It was, by all accounts, a modern fairy tale. Only this one seems to have ended with the prince being turned into a frog.

What started as a love story fit for the Instagram age has turned into the kind of cautionary tale you’d expect from a gossip magazine. Meghan, determined to rewrite royal history, thought she could take the charming prince, polish him up, and make him the face of a new brand. But in the process, she turned Harry—once everyone’s favourite, affable royal—into a man lost in a sea of podcast cancellations, slow-motion car ‘chases’, and public therapy sessions.

As for Meghan, the duchess who would modernise the monarchy, she quickly became better known for her rotating staff roster and pre-dawn emails than for any philanthropic deeds. Dubbed ‘Duchess Difficult’, she managed to clear out the palace quicker than Brexit negotiations. You have to hand it to her, though—who else could take a royal and transform him into a Hollywood house-husband doing mental health talks and fidgeting in interviews?

After all, it takes a certain kind of magic to convince a prince to turn his back on a literal kingdom in exchange for a deal with Spotify, only to have it go bust. And who could forget their $100 million Netflix ‘special’, where they spent hours recounting how tough life was inside royal palaces that most people would give their left arm to live in. Harry, once an army officer and people’s prince, now finds himself as a glorified extra in Meghan’s ongoing production of “Meghan’s World.”

The turning point must have been the New York ‘car chase’ debacle. He thought he was getting his happily-ever-after. Instead, he’s found himself as the frog in a very one-sided fairy tale, waiting for a kiss that will never come.

Consider the tale of her supposed close pals. There’s the loyal 𝘑𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘤𝘢 𝘔𝘶𝘭𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘺, who was once the poster child for Meghan’s inner circle. But after a minor social faux pas involving a controversial incident, Meghan decided that ghosting was in order. Just like that, Mulroney was left on read, a testament to Meghan’s precarious friendships. Who needs loyalty when you can simply cut ties with anyone who challenges your narrative?

Then there’s her frosty relationship with former castmates from 𝘚𝘶𝘪𝘵𝘴. Once a valued part of their ensemble, Meghan has exhibited all the warmth of a polar vortex since her ascent into royal life. When she didn’t receive the glowing endorsement she craved, she retreated into the shadows, leaving her former friends clutching their pearls in disbelief. They must have learned the hard way that Meghan’s concept of friendship is as fleeting as her time on the royal scene.

And while she appears to maintain a good rapport with 𝘚𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘢 𝘞𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘢𝘮𝘴 for now, one can’t help but wonder how long that will last. Their camaraderie may be intact at the moment, but if Serena fails to meet Meghan’s expectations or offer the unwavering support she craves, will she too become a ghost in Meghan’s social portfolio?

The reality is that Meghan’s approach to friendship resembles her approach to life: superficial and self-serving. If you don’t validate her choices or fall in line with her whims, you’re out. It’s a high-stakes game of emotional roulette where the odds are stacked against anyone who dares to disagree.

The irony, of course, is that Meghan has constructed a public persona as a champion of kindness and empathy. Yet, when it comes to her friendships, that facade disintegrates faster than a knock off designer handbag. Her behaviour reveals a troubling truth: she’s less interested in fostering genuine connections and more in curating a gallery of admirers who echo her sentiments and feed her ego.

In a world that celebrates authenticity, Meghan Markle has chosen the path of the fake friend, a spectre haunting her own social landscape. It’s high time for her to face the music and realise that true friendship is built on trust and respect, not on selective appearances and strategic disappearances. If she continues down this path, she may soon find herself entirely friendless—an empty castle with no one left to turn the lights on.

In the latest chapter of the Sussexes’ post-palace saga, the power couple known for “escaping” the royal family’s golden cage seems to have run into a bit of a gilded problem of their own. Enter 𝘐𝘯𝘛𝘰𝘶𝘤𝘩’s newest headline: “𝘋𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘎𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘥!”—not exactly the fairy-tale ending they had in mind when they departed Britain’s shores, proclamations of independence trailing behind them.

Let’s dissect this “$100 million empire collapse,” shall we? For two people who once bemoaned the scrutiny and pressures of being in the royal fishbowl, Harry and Meghan sure seemed to make a swift U-turn back into the spotlight, albeit a more lucrative one. Who knew privacy could be so profitable? Between lucrative Netflix deals, star-studded Spotify podcasts, and tell-all book advances, they proved that fame can indeed be sold by the pound—until, it appears, the empire built on grievances and carefully crafted victimhood narratives began showing some cracks.

“𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘉𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴! screams the subhead, as if the world needed reminding of their extravagances. For Harry, the young prince who once dared to tell the world his father had financially abandoned him (while living in a multimillion-dollar Montecito mansion), financial reality may now be arriving with the grace of a stagecoach collision. As for Meghan, the transformation from a self-styled humanitarian to the Duchess of Dollar Signs has not exactly gone unnoticed.

And now, it seems, the “reckless royals” have reached the inevitable end of their fairy tale: not with the pomp and pageantry they once denounced, but with headlines about their “𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴!” Yes, the allure of billionaire ambitions was just too tantalising to resist, even for those who claimed to be fleeing the trappings of aristocratic privilege. One might say their undoing wasn’t so much greed as a relentless pursuit of relevance—wrapped in the velvet of luxury and sprinkled with a hint of delusion.

So, as the Sussex empire teeters, perhaps this isn’t the fairy tale they envisioned when they traded Buckingham Palace for a Californian castle. Instead of newfound freedom, it seems they’ve simply exchanged one gilded cage for another—only this time, the bars are forged by ambition, avarice, and a ravenous pursuit of fame.

They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.

Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

author: @kansasrose2909
text:
𝐀 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐭𝐨𝐫: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲

Prince Harry, the lad who once charmed a nation, has managed quite the transformation: from beloved royal to poster boy for betrayal. In centuries past, he’d be dragged to the Tower with little ceremony, his name whispered with distaste over tankards of ale. Today, he basks in California sunshine, preaching authenticity while ghosting the very traditions that made him. Truly, a modern traitor for modern times.

For what else could we call a prince who has traded his duty for Netflix deals, swapped family loyalty for public therapy sessions, and thrown his heritage to the wind in favour of a victim narrative? Picture it: Harry, once a soldier in Afghanistan, now waging a different sort of war—a tireless battle against his own past, as he sits in his Montecito mansion. Gone are the days of duty and decorum; now it’s all about the next “revelation,” the next family gripe aired to anyone still willing to listen.

Of course, there’s Meghan, sharing in this saga as if they’re star-crossed lovers in a production of 𝘙𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘶𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘵: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. Together, they’ve built an empire on carefully curated angst, dressing up their defection as a noble quest for “freedom.” And yet, one can’t help but wonder if Harry’s “freedom” really amounts to little more than a gilded cage of their own making.

Meanwhile, back in Britain, Prince William quietly shoulders the legacy Harry discarded, preparing himself for kingship. His royal path is steady, measured—a role fulfilled with grace. Harry, on the other hand, seems more determined to stamp his name as a rogue prince, thumbing his nose at history as he clings to the fleeting rewards of his rebellion.

If Harry hoped to cement himself as some romantic figure, a maverick hero for the ages, he’s sorely mistaken. Instead, he’s  joined a long list of deserters and disgraced figures, his place in history etched not with respect but with regret. Because at the end of the day, there’s little noble in betrayal, no honour in disloyalty, and no lasting glory in the desertion of one’s own family. For a modern prince, he’s carved out a legacy steeped in treachery—one that history will neither forget nor forgive.
