text:
𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐧 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐞𝐨𝐩𝐥𝐞’𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐲𝐩𝐨𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐲

Oh, the irony. Here we have the Duke and Duchess of Sussex—those self-styled champions of “privacy” who fled the royal fold to pursue their “authentic” lives—caught in the act of their true pursuit: piles upon piles of cash. Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? They only wanted privacy from the obligations, it seems—not from the cash and cameras that come with the royal titles they claim to despise.

If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

author: @ocdman202
text:
𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐠𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧
Once upon a time, Meghan Markle declared she and Prince Harry were like “salt and pepper”—an inseparable pair set to add spice to the royal mix. Fast forward, and it’s hard to spot a single grain of that promised zest. The couple who vowed to blaze their own trail have instead become something of a rerun, replaying grievances that audiences tuned out long ago.

Their escape from royal life was billed as a grand breakaway, a daring move from palace to paradise, unshackled from outdated traditions. With the California sun casting its spotlight, it was their moment to be bold, maybe even trailblazing. But instead, we’ve been served a never-ending potluck of grievances. The memoir, the Netflix docuseries, the staged podcast series—all spoon-feed the same reheated drama to an audience that guessed the ending long ago.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬

What happened to the Sussexes' “fresh start”? The freedom they supposedly seized now looks more like a litany of complaints and nostalgia for a life they left behind. And those “truth bombs”? They’ve long since lost their impact. A touch of royal intrigue can be fun, but when every conversation turns back to old tensions and slights, the narrative grows tepid. The public saw through this act long ago; no one’s under the impression there’s any flavour left to savour.

𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐰𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 — 𝐀 𝐖𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞

Hollywood was their dream, a glitzy stage where they’d finally reveal their untethered selves. But that silver screen? It’s looking more like tinfoil. They may have imagined themselves as A-listers, but the reality has been a string of missed cues. Netflix and Spotify, hoping for fresh content, received thinly veiled tell-alls peppered with petty gripes. For a couple keen to “stand on their own,” the constant backtracking to royal family matters feels less like independence and more like clinging.

Instead of breaking new ground, Harry and Meghan have become supporting characters in their own saga, each episode diluted by yet another retelling. The world isn’t buying the drama, and any original sparkle has long since dulled.

𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

And here’s the kicker: while they shed titles in their “escape,” Harry and Meghan keep trotting out “The Duke and Duchess” when it suits them. Titles that once held gravitas now serve as branding props, miles away from the authenticity they touted. It’s all become a theatre of the obvious, a self-styled narrative playing out before a public well past caring.

Then there’s the irony of their ongoing privacy plea. Privacy-seekers don’t stage Netflix specials, pen tell-all books, or broadcast every charity visit. Each media appearance belies their claims, leaving them trapped in contradictions of their own making.

𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞

Meghan’s “salt and pepper” analogy now reads like satire. What once promised substance has become a dish over-seasoned with grievance, under-spiced with genuine creativity. They were supposed to break boundaries, not endlessly dine on past grievances. The world has moved on — and so should they. But, unable to escape their own stale narratives, the Sussexes are left to stew in a story that’s long since lost its flavour.

In the end, the Sussex saga just delivered a table set with an empty cruet set. As they continue to shake the same tired grievances, one thing is clear: the world has tasted all they have to offer—and doesn’t like the flavour.

In centuries past, he’d be dragged to the Tower with little ceremony, his name whispered with distaste over tankards of ale. Today, he basks in California sunshine, preaching authenticity while ghosting the very traditions that made him. Truly, a modern traitor for modern times.

For what else could we call a prince who has traded his duty for Netflix deals, swapped family loyalty for public therapy sessions, and thrown his heritage to the wind in favour of a victim narrative? Picture it: Harry, once a soldier in Afghanistan, now waging a different sort of war—a tireless battle against his own past, as he sits in his Montecito mansion. Gone are the days of duty and decorum; now it’s all about the next “revelation,” the next family gripe aired to anyone still willing to listen.

Of course, there’s Meghan, sharing in this saga as if they’re star-crossed lovers in a production of 𝘙𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘶𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘵: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. Together, they’ve built an empire on carefully curated angst, dressing up their defection as a noble quest for “freedom.” And yet, one can’t help but wonder if Harry’s “freedom” really amounts to little more than a gilded cage of their own making.

Meanwhile, back in Britain, Prince William quietly shoulders the legacy Harry discarded, preparing himself for kingship. His royal path is steady, measured—a role fulfilled with grace. Harry, on the other hand, seems more determined to stamp his name as a rogue prince, thumbing his nose at history as he clings to the fleeting rewards of his rebellion.

If Harry hoped to cement himself as some romantic figure, a maverick hero for the ages, he’s sorely mistaken. Instead, he’s  joined a long list of deserters and disgraced figures, his place in history etched not with respect but with regret. Because at the end of the day, there’s little noble in betrayal, no honour in disloyalty, and no lasting glory in the desertion of one’s own family. For a modern prince, he’s carved out a legacy steeped in treachery—one that history will neither forget nor forgive.

𝐀 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐓𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐢𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬

If we were to transpose Prince Harry’s behaviour to the time of our ancestors, the boy would find himself not in the opulent halls of a palace but rather in the dank confines of the Tower of London, languishing in chains. For in a bygone age, when treachery was dealt with by more than just the dubious appeasement of public opinion, he would have been dispatched to the tower quicker than you can say ‘traitor.’

Imagine the scene: a raucous court, gossip swirling like smoke from a Tudor fireplace. The nobles, their heads adorned with plumed hats, would shake their heads in disbelief, horrified at Harry’s audacity. This is a man who has squandered his royal birthright on a flimsy narrative of self-pity and the incessant drone of ‘me, me, me.’ Once the darling of the nation, he has plunged from grace faster than one of his cringe-inducing lectures.

The Tower, with its grim history of imprisoning those who dared to defy the crown, would be a fitting abode for our runaway prince. Here, amidst the echo of clanking chains and the occasional crow of a raven perched on the battlements, he would reflect on his many misdeeds—turning his back on a family steeped in tradition and duty. It is no exaggeration to say that he has become a masterclass in public disgrace, with a Netflix contract in hand and a penchant for revealing family secrets like a particularly scandalous Victorian novel.

Let us not forget the allies he has chosen—his wife, who seems intent on making headlines as though they were some sort of royalty-obsessed Kardashians, and a media machine that churns out sympathy pieces like a factory line of self-serving narratives. In the days of yore, such behaviour would have led to a one-way ticket to the Tower, where the only entertainment would be the occasional visit from the executioner, brandishing his axe with the same disdain the British public now holds for the Sussexes.

And who could blame us? Harry’s relentless parade of grievances—his childhood traumas, his estranged family, his perpetual victimhood—has grown tiresome. It feels as if he has taken the lessons of his late mother, Princess Diana, and turned them into a sordid reality show, where every episode is marked by betrayal and an insatiable need for public approval. One might argue that Diana, had she been around, would have given him a stern talking-to, perhaps even a ‘get a grip, Harry’ lecture over a cup of tea.

As he and Meghan traipse around the globe, preaching the virtues of mental health while simultaneously making a mockery of their own familial ties, one can’t help but wonder if their antics might prompt a royal edict—‘Let them eat cake’ as they sit in their ivory tower, oblivious to the discontent brewing below. For in this land of pomp and pageantry, where tradition is revered, their antics are as out of place as a jester in a cathedral.

Ultimately, Harry won’t find himself in the Tower, but perhaps it’s time to ponder the legacy he is crafting for himself—one of disgrace rather than distinction. In a world that once revered him, he now stands as a cautionary tale, a prince turned pauper of public opinion. It’s a royal disgrace that would make any self-respecting Prince shudder in their boots. If only he could hear the whispers of history echoing through the stone walls, reminding him that treachery, once committed, has a way of finding its just desserts.

𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐥 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐬

Prince Harry, once hailed as a ‘heroic’ soldier and proud Brit, now wants the world to believe his homeland is a hotbed of danger. He claims the UK is too perilous for his wife and children, a narrative as flimsy as his memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. But while he paints Britain as a dystopian nightmare, he and Meghan have no problem gallivanting off to actual high-risk countries like Colombia and Nigeria—places flagged by travel advisories for violent crime, terrorism, and kidnapping. It’s almost as if Harry’s “safety concerns” aren’t about safety at all, but rather a thinly veiled power play to strong-arm his way back into the protective bubble of royal security.

Let’s not forget the Sussexes' globe-trotting antics. Colombia and Nigeria, for example, are hardly the poster children for family tourism. Both nations are regularly flagged for extreme risks by the Foreign Office, with warnings about armed groups, kidnappings, and general lawlessness. And yet, there was Harry, happily jetting off with Meghan to these volatile regions without so much as a raised eyebrow. Of course, the kids stayed behind—as they always do. 

But when it comes to the UK—where royal protection has shielded generations from genuine threats—Harry’s tune suddenly changes. Britain, according to his narrative, is an inhospitable land teeming with danger, unfit for his children to step foot in unless the Sussexes are surrounded by elite security teams. Curious, isn’t it, how these so-called concerns about “safety” just happen to align with his ongoing legal battles for taxpayer-funded police protection? It’s almost as though Harry is holding his own country hostage, dangling the prospect of a royal return as leverage to get what he really wants: someone else footing the bill for his personal security detail.

The audacity is staggering. The UK isn’t a war zone. It’s not riddled with the risks Harry willingly courted when he traveled to regions like Nigeria and Colombia. No, the only “danger” Harry seems to fear is a lack of armed guards escorting him to private jets and red-carpet events. His claim that his family’s safety is at risk without police protection in the UK is not only disingenuous but also insulting to the intelligence of the British public. 

And let’s be honest—if safety were truly Harry’s priority, wouldn’t he be a little more cautious about trotting off to countries with 𝘢𝘤𝘵𝘶𝘢𝘭 risks of violence and terrorism? Wouldn’t he be more concerned about the optics of championing causes in unstable regions while dismissing the relative calm of his own homeland? But no, Harry and Meghan’s adventures in high-risk zones continue unabated, all while they use the UK’s supposed “dangers” as a convenient excuse to stay away and wage their battles from afar.

In reality, Harry’s “safety” narrative isn’t about his family at all. It’s about control. It’s about manipulating public perception and bending the system to suit his needs. By painting the UK as a land of doom and gloom, he’s attempting to pressure the establishment into reinstating the full-scale royal security he lost when he stepped back from his duties. It’s less about protecting his family and more about protecting his ego—and his wallet.

The British public sees through this charade. Harry’s safety excuses are as transparent as his PR strategy, and no amount of dramatic hand-wringing will change that. The truth is simple: the UK is not the dangerous place Harry wants us to believe it is. The only real threat is his unrelenting campaign to rewrite the rules to suit himself—and his increasingly flimsy grip on reality.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐮𝐱 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

When a narcissist’s brand starts to unravel, the signs are as blatant as the botox on their face. Take Meghan Markle, for instance—what was once a glitzy fairy tale is now a shambolic farce, complete with the melodrama of a daytime soap. The international press, once a willing accomplice, is sharpening its knives, churning out reports of her alleged bullying of staff. You’d think Meghan would take the hint, but instead, she seems intent on doubling down, wielding her victimhood narrative like a club to bash anyone who dares to cross her.

Let’s talk about hypocrisy for a moment. Harry and Meghan preach the need for safety on social media while simultaneously giving a free pass to their loyal supporters—who, let’s be honest, are more like rabid fans than followers. They’ve unleashed a horde of online bullies who terrorise anyone with the audacity to criticise the Sussexes. Meanwhile, pleas from journalists for the couple to rein in their toxic fanbase fall on deaf ears. Why would they care about accountability when playing the victim suits them so well? Their negligence is becoming a liability, and the public is beginning to take notice.

Despite their self-proclaimed social media absence (cough), the Sussex brand is experiencing a nosedive, with once-loyal fans jumping ship faster than you can say “spare.” Their recent attempt to regain relevance with a half-hearted conference in the U.S. was laughable at best, an embarrassing display of desperation that only highlighted their dwindling support.

And where are their Hollywood allies now? Oprah, Perry, Clooney—those who once rushed to their defence are conspicuously silent. The whispers about Netflix possibly dropping them have grown louder, echoing like a death knell for their carefully constructed empire. If anything, the lack of support is telling; it screams that the sheen has worn off, and the public is no longer buying what they’re selling.

Meghan’s flailing attempts to counteract the negative press with vapid puff pieces have only worsened her image. If given the chance, you can bet she’d jump at the opportunity for another Oprah-style interview, eager to spill her sob story for all to see. But here’s the kicker: when narcissists are cornered, they resort to more dramatic antics to reclaim their spotlight. Meghan’s recent appearance at the Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Gala was nothing short of a desperate bid for attention—a clear indication that the mask is slipping, and the facade is cracking.

As their influence wanes, Harry and Meghan are increasingly out of control, resorting to blame others for their failures. They’re losing key allies, as even the most die-hard supporters start to see through the artifice. It’s a slow-motion train wreck, with every misstep leading them further down the rabbit hole of irrelevance.

And let’s not forget the rumblings about their potential connection to the Diddy scandal. Could this be the final straw for their brand? The possibility of exposure for unethical or illegal activities might just put the finishing touches on their spectacular downfall.

In the end, the unraveling of a narcissist's brand is a dramatic spectacle, filled with chaos and disarray. As Meghan and Harry's carefully curated narratives crumble around them, they find themselves desperately trying to control a story that is slipping from their grasp. The truth is out there, and it’s starting to look a lot like the end of their fairy tale.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫 𝐢𝐧 𝐇𝐞𝐞𝐥𝐬: 𝐔𝐧𝐦𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐭: 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝟏

Isn’t it ironic how someone so intent on preaching kindness and compassion manages to leave chaos, misery, and a trail of broken spirits in her wake? Step into the twisted fairy tale of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Deceit, where behind the thin veneer of humanitarianism and “mental health advocacy” lies a woman now branded with more monikers than she can count. Whether we call her the Dictator in Heels, Princess Pinocchio, or the Duchess Difficult, one thing is clear—her reign has been far from the fairy tale she so desperately wants us to believe.

Let’s peel back the layers, shall we?

𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐬

The carefully constructed narrative that Meghan Markle wants us to buy is one of struggle, perseverance, and triumph. An actress on a cable TV show (𝘚𝘶𝘪𝘵𝘴, lest we forget, not exactly 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘺𝘸𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘢𝘭𝘵𝘺), she was once a nobody, waiting tables and fighting her way to stardom. But for those who worked with her before the royal wedding, it was less of a rise and more of a royal pain. While there were no formal complaints before she sashayed into Kensington Palace, whispers of her ‘high-maintenance’ behaviour circulated on set. A diva, some said. But hey, a few dramatic outbursts come with the territory of being a “leading lady,” right?

Then came her golden ticket: the royal family. What started as a fairy-tale romance quickly turned into a nightmare for those who had the misfortune of working for her.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

Let’s fast forward to 2018, just after the fairy-tale wedding to Prince Harry, where Meghan took up residence at Kensington Palace and reportedly made herself quite at home—at everyone else’s expense. In March 2021, 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘛𝘪𝘮𝘦𝘴 unleashed a bombshell report revealing bullying allegations against Meghan, dating back to her earliest days as the Duchess. Staff—those poor souls bound by duty and discretion—painted a chilling picture of life under her rule. She was, in their words, a nightmare who allegedly left personal assistants in tears, undermined their confidence, and drove more than a few to resign.

We don’t get the nickname Duchess Difficult for being warm and fuzzy, now do we?

Here we go again. Someone who has spent a lifetime wielding their privilege like a weapon now claims to be the “most bullied person in the world.” Spare us the theatrics. Perhaps if you had treated everyone you encountered—friends, family, and the unsuspecting public—with a smidge of kindness and humility, the global reaction might have been a tad more favourable. 

But no, instead you’ve opted for a personal brand of destruction that insults friends and family alike, emotionally abuses the elderly, and allegedly blackmails the royal family. If there’s a litany of bad behaviour that screams “victim,” yours is it. The entitlement you displayed when demanding to move into Windsor Castle or expecting the Australian Prime Minister to vacate his residence for your convenience is nothing short of staggering. The cheek! And let’s not even get started on your derisive comments about the accommodations provided by South African ministers during your jaunt there—how charming.

You’ve curated an online cult of cruelty that would make the worst schoolyard bully blush. Instead of fostering compassion, you’ve encouraged a toxic atmosphere of hate and ridicule, hounding your detractors with vicious, derogatory comments. It’s baffling how someone can be so ungracious while playing the victim card so shamelessly.

Then, there’s your cold dismissal treatment of your elderly father and siblings, an act so shockingly cruel it would make even the most hardened cynics wince. This pattern of rudeness, ingratitude, and self-aggrandisement is precisely why you’re met with derision and disdain. Yet, instead of taking a good hard look in the mirror and accepting responsibility, you deflect blame like a master escape artist.

Let’s cut to the chase: you are the architect of your own downfall. It’s time to put away the crocodile tears and stop the pity party. A true path to redemption requires humility, self-reflection, and a genuine apology to those you’ve wronged. But let’s be real—do you have it in you to transform from a self-styled diva into something resembling a decent human being? I doubt it. Even if you tried, the public would be hard-pressed to take you seriously. 

True change comes from acknowledging one’s flaws and making amends. Until you can do that, this tiresome narrative of victimhood will continue to ring hollow. You’ve played the part of the wronged party for too long, and it’s getting increasingly difficult to believe that the world is at fault for your woes. Look around—maybe, just maybe, the issue lies with you.

𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐍𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐦

In a world that seems to worship the grandiose, few individuals exemplify the essence of narcissism quite like Meghan Markle. The erstwhile actress, now the Duchess of Sussex, has turned her life into a perpetual performance, and we are all unwilling spectators in her ongoing melodrama.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐰𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝𝐲: 𝐂𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬!

From the moment she entered the royal spotlight, Meghan made it clear she intended to be the headline act. The Oprah Winfrey interview was a masterclass in self-pity, shifting the focus from the monarchy to her own perceived suffering. It’s as if she believes her struggles warrant a Netflix series—a tawdry soap opera filled with tears and accusations.

𝐂𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐂𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐬: 𝐋𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞!

Meghan has transformed the media into her personal soapbox, scripting her narrative like a desperate writer. She unleashes well-timed leaks to cast herself as the misunderstood outsider battling an archaic institution. Instead of rising to the occasion during royal turmoil, Meghan threw a tantrum on international television, crafting an image so far removed from reality it resembles fantasy.

𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐬? 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐈𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞!

In Meghan’s world, relationships are expendable. Her estrangement from her father and half-siblings reads like a bad drama. She keeps only those who serve her narrative, including her infamous rift with the royal family—an institution she clearly disdains. If she isn’t the centre of attention, she seems to lose interest, leaving a trail of broken connections.

𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠

Meghan’s relentless pursuit of fame is astounding. She traded royal duties for Hollywood deals faster than you can say “publicity stunt,” signing multi-million-pound contracts while lamenting her loss of privacy. Does she care for philanthropy, or is her true love the fleeting high of applause?

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐎𝐥𝐲𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐬: 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐏𝐢𝐭𝐲

While advocating for social issues, Meghan’s approach often feels like a marketing strategy rather than genuine concern. Each speech draws more attention to her trauma than the causes she claims to support. It’s hard to take seriously a woman who has lived in palaces while positioning herself as a martyr, using her platform for personal grievances rather than the greater good.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐟-𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 — 𝐀 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐆𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐠𝐞

Meghan Markle serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of narcissism. In her quest for independence and recognition, she has alienated herself from those who might offer her support. It begs the question: in a world filled with adoration and applause, will she ever find the genuine connections she seems so desperately to seek? For all her talk of freedom and authenticity, Meghan remains trapped in a gilded cage of her own making, where the pursuit of fame ultimately leaves her more isolated than ever.

And while the world watches her every move, one thing is certain: Meghan Markle is the star of her own show, and it’s a performance that reveals far more about her character than she would like to admit.

text:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲: 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞

Prince Harry, once the shining light of the royal family, has now become a figure of contempt in Britain, a man who has not only turned his back on his family but, more egregiously, sold out his country. His actions over the past few years have burned every last bridge, leaving the British public with nothing but scorn for the man who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the people.

The Oprah interview was the tipping point. It was here that Harry, complicit in silence, allowed Meghan Markle to imply that a member of the royal family had concerns about the skin colour of their son, Archie. The accusation was seismic, sending shockwaves through the UK. But what made this worse—what made it utterly unforgivable—was Harry’s inaction. His failure to stand up for his family while his ailing grandfather, Prince Philip, was in his final days showed a callous disregard for the pain it would cause. No matter the issues he may have had behind closed doors, to go on international television and sully the name of the institution that raised him was seen by many as nothing short of treachery.

And as if the Oprah debacle wasn’t bad enough, we were later subjected to 𝘏𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 & 𝘔𝘦𝘨𝘩𝘢𝘯, the Netflix mockumentary thinly veiled as a love letter to themselves but in truth, a very public airing of grievances. It was here that Meghan’s mocking of the royal tradition of curtsying to Queen Elizabeth shocked us Brits. With a poorly executed theatrical bow and a laughable comparison to medieval times, she belittled a gesture that symbolises respect and duty—values the British monarchy stands for. And Harry? He smirked. His silence, again, was deafening. How could any grandson, raised in the folds of such tradition, allow his wife to mock the woman who represented so much to so many?

The British people watched, aghast. That smirk—that quiet complicity—was a betrayal not just of his family, but of us, the British public who had once held him in such high regard. Queen Elizabeth, beloved and respected, was the embodiment of duty and grace, and for Harry to stand idly by as she was mocked before her passing will never be forgiven. The wound is deep, and it’s raw.

Then came the memoir 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦. If the Netflix series was a veiled attack, 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦 was an all-out assault. Page after page of grievances, personal attacks on his father and brother, intimate family moments laid bare for the world to see. The British public has always respected the monarchy’s ability to keep private matters within the palace walls. Harry tore that tradition apart. And for what? A quick buck, a bit of global attention. The title of ‘spare’ may have haunted him his whole life, but now it’s clear: the role he once resented is one he’s embraced—no longer a prince, but a spare to the very values that once defined him.

For us Brits, it isn’t just the content of his attacks that hurts—it’s the fact that he’s chosen to air them so publicly, so vindictively. The monarchy is not just his family; it is the backbone of British history, culture, and identity. To see it so easily discarded and vilified by one of its own is a wound that may never heal.

No, Britain will not forgive Harry. The man who was once the cheeky prince with a ready smile and a heart for service has become a symbol of betrayal. He has betrayed his family, his country, and his role in history. And for that, there is no going back.

𝟕𝟐 𝐇𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐲𝐫𝐝𝐨𝐦: 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞’𝐬 𝐌𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐢𝐫 𝐨𝐟 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐲

Oh, the irony! Meghan Markle, our ‘favourite’ Duchess of Dismay, is reportedly working on a tell-all memoir about her alleged 72 hours as a working royal. Yes, that’s right—three days in a tiara, and she’s convinced she has enough material to rival Shakespeare’s tragedies. I can hardly wait for the enlightening tales of adversity that surely await us. Spoiler alert: I suspect they’ll be as riveting as watching paint dry.

Let’s not forget that Meghan’s grand total of royal duties could hardly fill a pamphlet, yet she’s poised to regale us with her experiences as if she survived a shipwreck. In those fleeting 72 hours, she managed to squeeze in a handful of engagements before she and Harry were off, leaving behind a trail of baffled courtiers and one very confused corgi. But alas, this is the same woman who turned a mere two years in the spotlight into an epic saga of betrayal and emotional trauma. So why stop now?

What can we expect from this memoir? A deep dive into the horrors of royal life? A gripping narrative detailing the systemic oppression she faced from her fellow royals? I can only imagine the subheadings: “Chapter One: The Cruelty of Curtsying” and “Chapter Two: The Unbearable Weight of the Crown.” Truly, who knew tiaras could be so oppressive?

If her previous forays into storytelling are anything to go by, we can anticipate another round of victimhood, complete with dramatic retellings of her time in the palace. Perhaps she’ll recount the agonising moment when she discovered the palace didn’t come with a personal stylist or how she was forced to endure the trials of royal protocol while trying to navigate a world where she was expected to smile and wave.

But let’s be real. This memoir is destined to be another whinge-fest, a victim’s manifesto penned by a woman who spent more time on Instagram than she did attending royal events. Meghan will undoubtedly fill the pages with tales of how she was misunderstood, how her mental health was allegedly jeopardised by the stuffy traditions of the monarchy, and how she was forced to endure life with “difficult” people like the Queen and Prince Charles.

And of course, no memoir of hers would be complete without the obligatory accusations of racism and systemic cruelty. It’s the get out of jail free card in her narrative, allowing her to play the role of the wronged princess in a fairytale gone horribly awry. Who knew a three-day stint could come with so many grievances?

In the end, Meghan’s memoir will likely reflect more on her relentless quest for victimhood than any real insights into the workings of the royal family. If she really believes she can turn a brief royal experience into a bestseller, then bless her heart. I’d wager my hat that it’ll be yet another saga of self-pity dressed up as profound wisdom.

So, fasten your seatbelts, Meghan Markle is about to take us on yet another wild ride through her self-crafted narrative, and I have a feeling it’s going to be one heck of a predictable journey!

In the grand theatre of royal melodrama, it appears that Harry and Meghan have firmly established themselves as the chief protagonists of the blame game. Like clockwork, their monotonous dirge of complaints plays on a never-ending loop, each note dripping with self-pity and delusion. The attached cartoon, with its scathing "Mr & Mrs WAAAGH," perfectly encapsulates the emotional petulance that has come to define their public personas. 

It’s always 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺𝘣𝘰𝘥𝘺 𝘦𝘭𝘴𝘦'𝘴 𝘧𝘢𝘶𝘭𝘵 for the Sussexes, as they thrash and kick their way through each grievance, unable—or unwilling—to accept any responsibility for their own missteps. Perhaps it's the cold shoulder from their family, or the world’s failure to recognise the sheer brilliance of their global "mission." Or maybe it's just that those pesky royal protocols dared to exist, cramping their Hollywood aspirations. One minute they preach compassion from their Montecito mansion, and the next, they’re busy launching volleys of blame, alleging betrayal by family members they once claimed to love.

Let’s call it what it is: an ongoing temper tantrum of epic proportions, masked as noble defiance. Poor Harry, still stuck in a psychological headlock of “mummy issues” and a never-ending spiral of resentment. And Meghan, with her quivering lip and tearful declarations of being “𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘰𝘴𝘵 𝘣𝘶𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘥 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘪𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘭𝘥,” trots out every cliché in the victim playbook. Yet for a couple who loathe the monarchy, they seem perfectly happy to clutch onto their royal titles—when it suits them, of course.

The genius of this cartoon lies not just in its hilarious caricature of the couple flailing on the ground like children denied their latest toy, but in its profound truth. “Mr & Mrs WAAAGH!” indeed—forever wailing into the void about the injustices heaped upon them, with no self-awareness that their self-inflicted PR carnage has burned every bridge they once held dear.

For Harry, who once epitomised a cheeky, lovable royal, his descent into this abyss of public whining is nothing short of tragic. Gone are the days of the sturdy, stoic prince, replaced by a man seemingly addicted to grievance. And Meghan, well, Hollywood didn’t care before she found a prince, and the Palace seems to care even less now. The fairy tale is over, and in its place, we are left with the endless 𝘞𝘈𝘈𝘈𝘎𝘏 of a couple who simply cannot stop blaming the world for their downfall.

What the Sussexes fail to understand—perhaps because they are too busy casting stones—is that their attempts to shift the narrative only reinforce their image as spoiled, self-indulgent, and utterly tone-deaf. They sit atop their multimillion-dollar empire, professing victimhood, while the world looks on, exhausted by the unrelenting cries of "woe is me."

In the end, the cartoon's portrayal is spot on. There they are, Harry and Meghan, forever locked in a cycle of kicking and screaming, oblivious to the fact that the only people responsible for their misery are the ones staring back at them in the mirror.

𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐞’𝐬 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐄𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐞

The fairy tale is over, and the clock has struck midnight for Meghan Markle. Once the dazzling darling of American celebrity culture, she now finds herself the subject of ridicule as the media turns against her with a vengeance. The creators of 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘬 recently unleashed a scathing episode that gleefully skewered the couple’s relentless quest for fame, poking fun at their so-called “Worldwide Privacy Tour.” In a delightful twist of irony, Meghan and Harry were portrayed as self-absorbed fame-seekers, proving that their desire for privacy is as sincere as a Hollywood starlet’s tearful confession on a talk show.

Fuel to this flaming dumpster of derision was thrown by none other than Bill Simmons, a 𝘚𝘱𝘰𝘵𝘪𝘧𝘺 executive, who infamously branded the Sussexes as “f***ing grifters” during a podcast. This blunt assessment reflects the mounting frustration within the industry over their much-hyped partnership, which ended with a whimper rather than a bang. The glow of admiration that once surrounded Meghan has dimmed to a flickering candlelight of exasperation, with outlets now dissecting the reality behind her royal façade and celebrity ambitions with a newly sharpened scalpel.

Adding insult to injury, 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘺𝘸𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘙𝘦𝘱𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘳 has not held back in its criticism. Commentator John McWhorter has dubbed Meghan “Duchess Difficult,” and “Dictator in Heels.” Such monikers perfectly encapsulate the desperate attempts by the Sussexes to reshape the royal narrative while profiting handsomely from their supposed victimhood. Once embraced by the Hollywood elite, Meghan now faces a chorus of eye rolls and side glances that echo the sentiment: “Not you again.”

The full extent of Meghan’s fall from grace was laid bare at the Los Angeles Children’s Hospital event, where reports emerged that she was asked to leave. Yes, the once-glittering star was ejected from a charity gala designed to help children in need—an event that should have been a soft landing for her in the world of philanthropy. Instead, it served as a glaring reminder that she has become persona non grata in the very circles that once admired her. When even a gala dinner aimed at children can’t tolerate your presence, it’s time to rethink your approach to celebrity.

And yet, amid this American backlash, the British media continues to shower the Sussexes with the kind of affection usually reserved for long-lost royals. Why the disconnect? It’s a perplexing puzzle, considering the British tabloids have historically thrived on scandal and sensationalism. Perhaps the allure of a royal couple willing to spill family secrets and criticise the institution is just too tempting for them to resist, even as their American counterparts have grown weary of the spectacle.

One must wonder whether the British media is simply chasing clicks and profits or if they’ve confused their roles as royal correspondents for cheerleaders in a bizarre, never-ending pageant. After all, nothing sells like royal drama wrapped in celebrity glitter, and the Sussex saga is the gift that keeps on giving.

One can only marvel at their ability to ignore the growing disdain from across the pond while indulging in the latest scandal with enthusiasm. The question remains: are they genuinely invested in the royal family or merely opportunists ready to feast on the scraps of gossip that fall from the Sussexes’ table?

As the Sussex saga continues, it’s clear the royal couple now teeters on a precarious edge. The image they once sought to project is increasingly battered by a growing backlash. With the ground shifting rapidly beneath them, they may soon realise that the world they once tried to dominate has moved on, leaving them to navigate the fallout of their own making.

Is it just me, or is there something utterly absurd about Harry and Meghan’s claim to integrity? While they love to rail against the media, they’ve turned it into their personal stage for airing grievances and sharing details best kept behind closed doors. Their high-profile chat with Oprah felt more like a prime-time soap opera than a royal disclosure, exposing family matters with all the decorum of a reality show. Trust? That’s long gone.

How can we take their complaints about media intrusion seriously when they’ve wielded the press like a weapon, crafting a narrative that’s equal parts victimhood and self-promotion? They’ve laid bare their lives in the most scandalous way imaginable, creating a spectacle out of what should have been private. It’s as if they’ve mistaken the royal family for a Netflix series, where ratings trump reality and the family business is mere entertainment.

Let’s talk about those awards, shall we? Harry’s got a Ripple of Hope Award and a shiny spot in the Living Legends of Aviation Hall of Fame. Royalty, traditionally the bestowers of honours, now seems to have entered a bizarre game of musical chairs where everyone gets a trophy for merely existing. Meanwhile, his antics and self-serving behaviour overshadow any merit these accolades might have.

The public’s reaction? Well, it’s as divided as ever. Some lap up their revelations, while others are left cringing at the sheer hypocrisy. Their willingness to exploit their royal status while claiming victimhood is a masterclass in contradiction.

And let’s not forget Harry’s military background—a legacy of service that now feels tarnished by his endless pursuit of fame. Instead of honouring that heritage, he seems hell-bent on dismantling it, trading dignity for headlines.

In the end, the combination of their media theatrics and the audacity of their royal status has cultivated a sense of betrayal that’s hard to shake off. If integrity were a currency, Harry and Meghan are already bankrupt.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐱 𝐄𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐞: 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐨𝐧 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞, 𝐓𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝

In the latest chapter of the Sussexes’ post-palace saga, the power couple known for “escaping” the royal family’s golden cage seems to have run into a bit of a gilded problem of their own. Enter 𝘐𝘯𝘛𝘰𝘶𝘤𝘩’s newest headline: “𝘋𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘺𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘎𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘥!”—not exactly the fairy-tale ending they had in mind when they departed Britain’s shores, proclamations of independence trailing behind them.

Let’s dissect this “$100 million empire collapse,” shall we? For two people who once bemoaned the scrutiny and pressures of being in the royal fishbowl, Harry and Meghan sure seemed to make a swift U-turn back into the spotlight, albeit a more lucrative one. Who knew privacy could be so profitable? Between lucrative Netflix deals, star-studded Spotify podcasts, and tell-all book advances, they proved that fame can indeed be sold by the pound—until, it appears, the empire built on grievances and carefully crafted victimhood narratives began showing some cracks.

“𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘉𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴! screams the subhead, as if the world needed reminding of their extravagances. For Harry, the young prince who once dared to tell the world his father had financially abandoned him (while living in a multimillion-dollar Montecito mansion), financial reality may now be arriving with the grace of a stagecoach collision. As for Meghan, the transformation from a self-styled humanitarian to the Duchess of Dollar Signs has not exactly gone unnoticed.

And now, it seems, the “reckless royals” have reached the inevitable end of their fairy tale: not with the pomp and pageantry they once denounced, but with headlines about their “𝘈𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘪𝘳𝘦𝘴!” Yes, the allure of billionaire ambitions was just too tantalising to resist, even for those who claimed to be fleeing the trappings of aristocratic privilege. One might say their undoing wasn’t so much greed as a relentless pursuit of relevance—wrapped in the velvet of luxury and sprinkled with a hint of delusion.

So, as the Sussex empire teeters, perhaps this isn’t the fairy tale they envisioned when they traded Buckingham Palace for a Californian castle. Instead of newfound freedom, it seems they’ve simply exchanged one gilded cage for another—only this time, the bars are forged by ambition, avarice, and a ravenous pursuit of fame.

𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐲 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫

Once upon a time, a prince with a shiny title and a Hollywood hopeful with dollar signs in her eyes found each other and decided to live out their own ‘fairy tale’, far from the stuffy conventions of royal life. They ditched it all—the tiaras, the castles, and the life of unimaginable privilege—along with the tiresome public appearances—to carve out a niche in the land of life coaches, wellness cults, and fame-hungry A-listers. Yet somewhere between the Netflix deals and the wellness podcasts, their dream of “happily ever after” began to wither. Now, Harry and Meghan find themselves trapped in the palace of their nightmares, stranded in the gilded mediocrity of Montecito.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐨𝐦—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐞

To Harry, stepping back from the royal family felt like a brave act of rebellion—a bid to escape his brother’s shadow, live life on his own terms. For Meghan, it was a chance to merge royal protocol with red carpet glitz, playing the part of modern duchess on a global stage. Except, it turns out, the world beyond the palace walls is tougher than they anticipated. Out there, far from the gates of Buckingham Palace, they found themselves face-to-face with the public’s dwindling patience—and, of course, that relentless mortgage..

They thought they were trading titles for freedom; instead, they traded them for endless self-promotion. No longer tied to the family firm, they are now forever bound to the grind of brand-building, constantly selling an image of authenticity that’s beginning to wear thin.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 ‘𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞’ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐲

Once, their narrative was fresh—a tale of liberation from an antiquated monarchy. But “their truth,” as they insist on calling it, soon became yesterday’s news. The Oprah interview, the Netflix docuseries, the podcasts—they were supposed to be explosive but fizzled out as just more of the same. Every grievance repeated, every “bombshell” a rehash. The audience that once embraced them as ‘victims’ began to see them as something altogether different: not underdogs, but opportunists who, in their haste to tell “their side,” had somehow forgotten that less can sometimes be much, much more.

For Meghan, the Hollywood dream always seemed tantalisingly close—a chance to transform herself from cable TV actress to A-list royalty. But Hollywood, as it turns out, wasn’t quite as enchanted with Meghan as she was with it. And for Harry, the harsh reality set in that once you remove the royal mystique, you’re just another person with opinions, a nice house, and some peculiar ideas.

𝐀 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐮𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫

And let’s not forget the family drama that unfolds like a soap opera on an endless loop. Harry and William, once the picture of closeness, are now estranged, a rift that seems destined to deepen. For Meghan, her fairy tale of becoming part of the Windsor family dissolved into a tabloid reality far from the idyllic promise. Their grievances, aired repeatedly across all channels, have been met by the royal family with an iron silence that has proven more powerful than a thousand tell-alls. What was once a family issue became a public spectacle, with Harry and Meghan marooned in their California mansion, squinting through the sunlit haze to discern why everyone seems so unmoved by “their truth.”

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐫—𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐒𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐲

So, here we are, at the “miserably ever after.” Harry and Meghan, no longer the royal rebels they once seemed but rather wannabe celebrities stuck in a loop of their own making. In their quest to set the record straight, they’ve only deepened the mystery: who are they really? And what exactly do they want? The fairytale gloss has faded, leaving them stranded in a life that looks more like a cautionary tale than a charming romance.

Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? They only wanted privacy from the obligations, it seems—not from the cash and cameras that come with the royal titles they claim to despise.

If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐠𝐡𝐚𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐬

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have found themselves in a peculiar position, attempting to fashion a life of American royalty. It’s a laughable endeavour, particularly for a couple that fled to America under the pretense of seeking freedom from royal duty—only to realise they were rejected by the very Hollywood they sought to embrace.

𝐀 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐞

Let’s cut to the chase: America has no use for royalty. The nation was forged in the spirit of independence and self-reliance, yet Harry and Meghan seem to have missed the memo. They have attempted to declare themselves as America’s answer to the royal family, but this self-proclaimed status is as welcome as a bull in a china shop.

After stepping back from royal duties, they made a beeline for Los Angeles, ready to conquer the American entertainment industry. To their dismay, Hollywood did not roll out the red carpet. Instead, they found themselves sidelined, their initial allure fading faster than Meghan’s acting career. The allure of royal heritage doesn’t hold much weight in America.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐥𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞

What’s particularly galling about their pursuit of status is the sheer hypocrisy that drips from every move they make. They preach about the importance of mental health and social justice, yet they reside in a mansion that screams privilege. Their glossy brand of activism is reminiscent of a Hollywood film script—polished but lacking genuine connection.

Their foundation, Archewell, is presented as a beacon of hope, yet it feels more like a vehicle for self-aggrandisement than true philanthropy. Their lives have become a never-ending PR campaign, hoping to cultivate an image that resonates with the public. But here’s the kicker: it’s transparent, and people see through it.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Harry and Meghan’s delusion of grandeur only deepens as they navigate this new world. They may fancy themselves as the new American royalty, but the truth is that their grandiose ambitions have been met with indifference. The public isn’t clamouring for their opinions or seeking their endorsement on social issues. Instead, they are the subjects of mockery, the unwelcome guests at a party they weren’t invited to.

In a country that embraces individualism, their attempts to establish themselves as a royal couple are met with laughter. Their attempts to assert themselves as important figures are a stark reminder that the American people have no need for a modern-day fairy tale featuring a couple so out of touch.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐀𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

In the end, Harry and Meghan’s aspirations to claim a space in American society as royalty are not only misguided—they are patently absurd. Their royal titles may remain, but in America, titles mean nothing. The essence of royalty is tied to duty, service, and, dare we say, sacrifice—all of which they seem to have cast aside in favour of self-promotion.

As they navigate their manufactured identities, it becomes painfully clear that the couple is merely grasping at straws. Let them parade their aspirations, but let it be known: America has enough self-made royalty to contend with. They don’t need another pair of out-of-touch aristocrats attempting to rewrite the narrative.

Oh, the irony. Here we have the Duke and Duchess of Sussex—those self-styled champions of “privacy” who fled the royal fold to pursue their “authentic” lives—caught in the act of their true pursuit: piles upon piles of cash. Prince Harry, grinning like a Cheshire cat, cracks a whip with all the enthusiasm of a ringmaster orchestrating his own spectacle, while Meghan clutches a bulging sack of money, her grin an unmistakable sign of how far she’s come from cable TV to the centre of a money-making circus.

And lying beneath this grand parade, the ghostly presence of Princess Diana—“The People’s Princess”—whose memory Harry has used justify his treachery. The very mother he claims to honour, positioned here as a quiet, helpless spectator in the spectacle he’s made of her legacy. Diana, who genuinely connected with people and dedicated herself to causes that meant something, now finds her image entangled in the cash-fuelled carnival Harry and Meghan have orchestrated in her name.

With banknotes and gold coins cascading like confetti, you can practically hear the ka-ching echoing through Montecito. From Netflix docuseries to tell-all memoirs, the Sussex duo has turned “public service” into “personal profit.” Privacy? They only wanted privacy from the obligations, it seems—not from the cash and cameras that come with the royal titles they claim to despise.

If Diana were here, she’d give her son a royal dressing-down for exploiting her memory to line his own pockets. Because for all Harry’s posturing, he’s not walking in his mother’s footsteps; he’s trampling on her memory.

Does Meghan Markle Want Us To Hate Her?
By: Madeline Osburn
January 06, 2025 
When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project?
There are plenty of reasons to hate Meghan Markle, so why did she just give us a whole Netflix season of more ammo? From stabbing the royal family in the back after having her entire life subsidized by British taxpayers to earning $25 million from Spotify for a few middling podcast episodes, Markle is a villainous figure who rakes in hate, not the praise and fandom she is clearly desperate for.

When Markle made her grand return to Instagram this New Year after dramatically quitting social media in 2021, it wasn’t for funsies. It was to announce and promote her new eight-part Netflix show, “With Love, Meghan.”
From the teaser trailer she shared, the series appears to be Markle’s best attempt at LARPing Martha Stewart with her celebrity pals on her $15 million Montecito compound. “I’m going to share some tips and tricks,” Markle says as she peruses the flower market and sprinkles dried flowers on top of glazed donuts.

“We’re not in the pursuit of perfection. We’re in the pursuit of joy!” she exclaims with an acute degree of inauthenticity. The copy is dripping with feigned platitudes and the images are suspiciously rife with royal ripoffs. This trailer is so cringe-inducing that it physically makes my eyes twitch.

What’s most surprising about this product is that there was no one close enough to her to wave their hands and gently guide her in the complete opposite direction. When Netflix came knocking, what pitches did she turn down when she opted for this Ballerina Farm wannabe vanity project? Did no one who loves her suggest a series with a bit more sympathetic angle? A reality show where she helps down-and-out folks find a new home? A docu-series where she visits small, but beautiful American cities, highlighting everyday heroes?

I’m just shooting from the hip, and these may not be streaming hits, but the fact that no one close to her advised her against her casual yet glamourous homemaker shtick (or they did and she didn’t listen) says a lot about the type of person she surrounds herself with. Ironically, that’s also what we mainly learn from the teaser trailer guest list — that Markle spends her time arranging flowers and beekeeping with some of the most affluent and out-of-touch celebrities in her Hollywood bubble. “This is probably one of the most glamourous moments of my life,” gushes Mindy Kaling.
And it’s important to clarify here that the snobbery does not come from the idea of picture-perfect homemaking. This type of nearly unattainable farm-to-table perfection is what skyrocketed and sustained Martha Stewart, Ina Garten, Ballerina Farm, and waves of Instagram influencers following in their footsteps. Women do not loathe these women for their ideas or talents. We gobble them up and strive to emulate their recipes and cabinet paint colors in our own kitchens. No, it’s the laughable idea that the privileged princess, the Hollywood actress-turned-diva-sister-in-law, and royal golddigger who excommunicated her husband from his family, is someone we trust as a source for bringing joy and life into our own homes.

The only plausible explanation for Markle’s vanity project is that she relishes victimhood so much that she doesn’t care what the haters say because their critiques and comments sustain her signature victim mentality. Knowing she will never be the beloved people’s princess like her late mother-in-law, she’s stopped trying and settled for the loathed queen of Montecito.

author: @AliceMoon-e2f
text:
09.01.2025 - Day of Princess Catherine 🎉🎉🎉
Sticky Toffee Pudding is said to be a favorite dessert of the royal family and a quintessentially British treat. Here’s a recipe fit for celebrating the Day of Princess Catherine!

Ingredients:

For the pudding:
	•	225g (8 oz) chopped dates
	•	200ml (7 fl oz) boiling water
	•	1 tsp bicarbonate of soda
	•	85g (3 oz) unsalted butter, softened
	•	140g (5 oz) dark brown sugar
	•	2 large eggs
	•	175g (6 oz) self-raising flour
	•	1 tsp vanilla extract

For the toffee sauce:
	•	200ml (7 fl oz) double cream
	•	100g (3.5 oz) dark brown sugar
	•	85g (3 oz) unsalted butter
	•	1 tbsp black treacle or golden syrup

Instructions:
	1.	Prepare the Dates:
	•	Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
	•	Place the dates in a bowl, pour over the boiling water, and stir in the bicarbonate of soda. Set aside for 10 minutes.
	•	Mash the dates with a fork until smooth.
	2.	Make the Batter:
	•	Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
	•	Gradually beat in the eggs, one at a time, then add the vanilla extract.
	•	Fold in the flour, then gently mix in the mashed dates.
	3.	Bake:
	•	Pour the batter into a greased and lined square baking dish or individual ramekins.
	•	Bake for 25-30 minutes (or 20 minutes for ramekins) until risen and springy to the touch.
	4.	Make the Toffee Sauce:
	•	In a small saucepan, combine the cream, sugar, butter, and treacle.
	•	Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 2-3 minutes until thickened.
	5.	Serve:
	•	Poke small holes in the pudding and pour over half the toffee sauce to soak in.
	•	Serve warm with the remaining sauce on the side, and a dollop of clotted cream or vanilla ice cream.

Toast to the Princess!

This indulgent dessert is a perfect way to honor Princess Catherine—a sweet, elegant treat for an extraordinary day. 🥂 Long live the Princess of Wales! 🥂

text:
Prince Harry — The Pinnacle of Media Manipulation and Hypocrisy

In an era where media manipulation has become alarmingly sophisticated, one individual stands out for his audacious exploitation of the press. With a blend of hypocrisy and calculated deceit, he has used various traditional platforms to advance his personal agenda while vociferously denouncing the very media he relies upon. His actions—particularly his constant invocation of his late mother’s name, the promotion of his book *Spare*, and his recent claim about Queen Elizabeth II—reveal the depths of his moral duplicity.

His memoir ‘Spare’ exemplifies his manipulative tactics. The book portrays him as a victim of media excess and royal intrigue, with every media appearance and promotional effort designed to capitalise on his grievances. This reliance on media exposure, which he simultaneously criticises, creates a hypocritical cycle of exploitation and condemnation.

A particularly egregious example of this manipulation was his claim on the programme ‘Tabloids On Trial’. During the show, he asserted that Queen Elizabeth II—who passed away in 2022—had supported him in his campaign against the media. The audacity of invoking a deceased monarch to bolster his narrative, despite her inability to refute or clarify his claims, reveals a staggering level of moral bankruptcy. This exploitation of his grandmother’s legacy is not merely about garnering sympathy; it is a calculated effort to manipulate public perception and advance his agenda.

By persistently invoking his family’s names, he cynically leverages their legacies to lend credibility to his assertions. Exploiting deceased individuals who cannot contest his claims is a deliberate and calculated ploy to shape public sentiment. It underscores the disturbing extent to which he is willing to go to achieve his objectives, all while maintaining a façade of fighting against media injustice.

In essence, his behaviour epitomises profound hypocrisy. He denounces the press for its supposed biases while simultaneously manipulating every available outlet—to serve his own ends. His ability to distort narratives and exploit personal tragedies for personal gain reveals a troubling pattern of deception. The real question remains: how much lower will he sink in his quest for validation and revenge, regardless of the cost to truth and decency?

author: @ocdman202
text:
The Duke of Sussex, our very own Prince Harry, forever ensconced in his Californian fortress of wokeness, emerges periodically to remind us of his perpetual state of existential dread. His latest missive, delivered with the gravitas of a man who believes he is one ill-advised soundbite away from Armageddon, once again revolves around his incessant fears regarding security. Yet, in this familiar narrative of peril, there lies a curious omission that even the most casual observer cannot fail to notice. 

Why, one wonders, does he never mention his dear children, those apple-cheeked cherubs who must surely feature prominently in his concerns for safety? No, in Harry's tale of impending doom, it is always Meghan, his duchess, his guiding star, who stands as the singular focus of his protective instincts. One could be forgiven for assuming that Archie and Lilibet, those innocents born into the Montecito soap opera, are perhaps spirited away to a secure undisclosed location every time Harry's security detail is the topic du jour. 

Is it possible, dare I say, that Harry's paternal instincts are overshadowed by his incessant need to shield Meghan from the predatory gaze of the paparazzi and the tabloid vultures? Or is this yet another chapter in the interminable saga of their beleaguered love story, where the perils of fame and the spectre of Diana's tragic fate are wheeled out to elicit a collective sigh from the global audience? 

In the grand theatre of their public pronouncements, one can't help but notice how the narrative is carefully scripted. Meghan is always the damsel in distress, while Harry, clad in the metaphorical armour of a modern-day Lancelot, valiantly fights off the demons of their shared notoriety. And the children? Well, perhaps they are tucked safely away in a nursery, blissfully unaware of their parents' ceaseless battle against the forces of darkness.

It's almost as if Harry's anxieties are a bespoke garment, tailored exclusively for Meghan, leaving one to wonder whether the children are considered less vulnerable, or simply less marketable, in this never-ending drama. 

But who are we to question the priorities of the Duke and Duchess? In their world, perhaps the greatest security threat is the one that jeopardises their perpetual narrative of victimhood. And in this theatre of the absurd, the children, it seems, play only a supporting role.

When and if the kids ever come out,  will we even care?

⚠ The Decline of the Invictus Games: From Respected Platform to PR Stunt ‼ 

Let’s be honest—what was once a meaningful and respected initiative has turned into a shameless PR parade, thanks to the Man-Child Harry and his D-List Social Climber wife Meghan Markle. The Invictus Games, originally created to honor and empower wounded service members, have been hijacked by a couple who seem far more interested in promoting themselves than the cause.  

Instead of focusing on veterans, the Games have become Meghan’s designer-clad runway, complete with shallow photo ops that scream “Look at me!” more than “Support our heroes.” The mission of Invictus—celebrating resilience and unity—has been overshadowed by a vanity project designed to boost their tarnished reputations. It’s insulting to the veterans who deserved better than to be props in this spectacle.  

And now, Harry wants to bring Invictus into schools? Spare us. His Vancouver appearance to promote the “Invictus Games School Program” wasn’t about inspiring kids—it was another desperate ploy to fix his approval ratings. Let’s not pretend this is about “the next generation.” This is about Harry trying to make himself look good while ignoring the obvious: his credibility is in the gutter.  

The irony is rich. Harry—privileged, out of touch, and with zero real-world experience—lecturing us about service, family, and children? No thanks. Veterans and parents alike are fed up with his constant preaching. And using kids as a PR shield to deflect from the Games’ declining support? That’s a new low. Here’s a message for Harry: LEAVE OUR KIDS ALONE! 

The Invictus Games used to stand for something noble—a symbol of respect for those who served. Now it’s bogged down by financial mismanagement, trust issues, and the polarizing presence of this fame-hungry duo. Veterans deserve so much better than having their platform co-opted by a Man-Child and his Social Climber wife, who shamelessly exploit their sacrifices to stay relevant.  

It’s time for Invictus to return to its roots: empowering veterans—not boosting the egos of those who have tarnished its cause. Enough is enough.

𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲: 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲’𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐠𝐞

In the pages of 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘦, Prince Harry makes a peculiar declaration: he doesn’t want to know anything about his family’s history. This statement, an odd mix of detachment and entitlement, raises eyebrows. Here we have a prince who seems to reject his own lineage while happily airing his grievances on a global stage.

One would think that a member of the royal family, steeped in centuries of history, would take an interest in the tales of his ancestors—their trials and tribulations, the complexities of royal life. Instead, Harry opts for a selective amnesia, as if ignorance will somehow absolve him from the consequences of his own actions. What a curious contradiction: he’s eager to spill the family secrets while simultaneously denying the very roots that define him.

This declaration becomes even more perplexing when considering Harry’s current situation. He’s abandoned his royal duties for a life in California, all while insisting on being a victim of a system he seems intent on dissecting. He doesn’t want to learn about the history of a family that has shaped the world. Yet he’s all too willing to exploit the drama of his personal history, using it as fodder for book deals and Netflix specials. It’s the epitome of hypocrisy.

By shunning his family history, Harry places himself in a troubling position. It’s as if he thinks he can rewrite his narrative without acknowledging the legacy attached to it. His ancestors’ stories are rich with triumph and tragedy—experiences that could provide valuable context for his own life. Instead, he chooses to dismiss them, a choice that reeks of privilege and ignorance.

In a world where family history can offer insights and understanding, Harry’s dismissal is not just odd but irresponsible. It signals a man adrift, refusing to learn from those who came before him. If he spent less time vilifying his family and more time understanding them, he might find a sense of belonging beyond the transient appeal of celebrity.

Perhaps it’s time for Harry to put down the soapbox, step into the archives, and embrace the history he so fervently rejects. Ignoring his roots won’t lead to the clarity he seeks; it will only deepen the chasm between him and the legacy that is his birthright.

8 types of workplace bullies:

The Screaming Mimi: Loud and obnoxious, this bully berates and humiliates coworkers and is motivated by hostility, causing stress and anxiety wherever they go.

The Gatekeeper: This worker exerts control by allowing or denying access to the tools — time, funds, supplies — you need to do your job. They enjoy the power of being in charge of resources and won’t let you forget it.

The Attention Seeker: Always trying to be the center of attention, this bully works hard to get on their manager’s good side and appear kind and helpful to teammates. But they’ll turn on you if they believe you’re not giving them the regard they deserve.

The Wannabe: This employee likes to be seen as indispensable but doesn't have the skills or expertise to make it on their own, so they hinder more competent coworkers to make themselves look good. If that strategy doesn’t work, they find the smallest details to complain about.

The Guru: A high performer in their area of expertise, The Guru suffers from an over-inflated sense of self-importance. They have no consideration for their fellow workers and won’t accept the possibility of being wrong.

The Sociopath: This bully is charming, intelligent, and well-spoken, which allows them to quickly advance to an upper management position. But they lack empathy and will manipulate your emotions, scheme, gaslight, and defame you to get what they want.
